The strategy covers every acceptance test in the DEFINE (AT-001 through AT-012): AT-001/006/007/008/009/010 map to backend integration tests; AT-002–005 map to backend unit tests (rejection) and frontend component tests (validation-state rendering); AT-011/AT-012 map to frontend component tests for the empty and request-failure states; the Playwright flow exercises AT-001, AT-007, AT-008, AT-009 together as a real user journey.

---

## Error Handling

| Error Type | Handling Strategy | Retry? |
|------------|-------------------|--------|
| Pydantic validation failure (bad title/description/status) | FastAPI returns 422 with a structured error body; frontend renders it as an inline validation-error state on the form | No |
| Task id not found (GET/PATCH/DELETE) | Router raises `HTTPException(404)`; frontend shows a not-found message for that action | No |
| Network failure / backend unreachable / 5xx | API client catches the fetch rejection or non-2xx status and returns a typed `ApiError`; frontend shows a top-level request-failure banner with a retry action | Yes — user-triggered retry via the same `refetch()` |
| Unexpected server exception | FastAPI's default 500 handler returns a generic JSON error; treated identically to the network-failure case on the frontend (no internal detail leaked) | No |

---

## Configuration

| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|------------|------|---------|--------------|
| `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` | string (env var) | `backend/data/taskflow.db` | SQLite file path; overridden to a temp path in tests |
| `TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` | string (env var, comma-separated) | `http://localhost:5173` | Origins allowed to call the API (the local Vite dev server) |
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | string (frontend env var) | `http://localhost:8000` | Base URL the frontend API client targets |

---

## Security Considerations

- No authentication/authorization is implemented — explicitly out of scope; the app is intended for a single local user on their own machine only, never exposed beyond `localhost`.
- All SQL is generated via SQLAlchemy's parameterized query construction — no string-formatted SQL anywhere, eliminating SQL injection risk (Decision 1).
- Pydantic validates and rejects malformed/oversized input before it reaches the database layer, bounding request-body size implicitly via the 120/500-character field limits.
- CORS is restricted to the known local dev origin via `TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` rather than left wide open (`*`).
- The SQLite file is `.gitignore`d so no local task data is ever committed to version control.

---

## Observability

| Aspect | Implementation |
|--------|----------------|
| Logging | FastAPI/Uvicorn's default structured access + error logging to stdout; no additional logging infrastructure needed for a local single-user tool |
| Metrics | None — out of scope; no operational metrics pipeline exists or is needed for a locally run tool with no deployment target |
| Tracing | None — out of scope for the same reason |

---

## Pipeline Architecture

Not applicable — TaskFlow is a single-table CRUD application, not a data pipeline, ETL process, or analytics workload. No DAG, partitioning, incremental strategy, or data-quality-gate sections apply.

file.content:
# Local Agents — Override AgentSpec

Agents in this directory **take precedence over AgentSpec plugin agents**
of the same name. Use this to customize phase agents to your project's
conventions without forking the plugin.

## Layout

| Folder | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `workflow/` | Override SDD phase agents (`brainstorm-agent`, `define-agent`, `design-agent`, `build-agent`, `ship-agent`, `iterate-agent`) |
| `custom/` | New project-specific agents that don't replace anything |

## Override an AgentSpec agent

1. Find the plugin agent at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/agents/<category>/<name>.md`
2. Copy it to `.claude/agents/<category>/<name>.md` — keep the `name:` field identical
3. Edit freely; your version is now what runs

Example: override `build-agent` so `/build` runs your team's review checklist:

```bash
cp $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/agents/workflow/build-agent.md \
   .claude/agents/workflow/build-agent.md
# edit .claude/agents/workflow/build-agent.md
```

## Add a custom agent

Drop a new `.md` file in `custom/` with valid frontmatter (`name`, `description`,
`tools`). It becomes available to `/build` and other phase commands automatically.

## Resolution Order

```text
.claude/agents/<name>.md   (your local override — wins)
        ↓ if absent
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/agents/<name>.md   (AgentSpec plugin)
```

This is enforced by Claude Code's native plugin loader. No config required.

Context — what this app must do (from sdd/features/DEFINE_TASKFLOW.md, read it for full detail):
- CRUD + search + filter + status workflow (todo/doing/done, default todo) over a single `tasks` resource.
- Title required after trim, 1-120 chars; description optional, <=500 chars; status restricted to the 3 values.
- Data must survive an app restart (SQLite file on disk).
- Search matches title+description case-insensitively; filter returns only the requested status.
- Frontend: works at desktop+mobile widths, no page reloads, accessible labels, distinguishes all statuses (not by color alone), and has loading/empty/validation/request-failure states.
- Invalid inputs (whitespace-only title, title >120, description >500, unknown status) must be rejected; a missing task must 404.
- No auth, no multi-user, no deployment, no external DB.

Also read sdd/features/DESIGN_TASKFLOW.md for the intended architecture/decisions, so you can flag any place the code deviates from its own stated design without justification.

For each finding give: severity, one-sentence description, exact file:line location, and why it matters (ideally tie it to a specific DEFINE requirement/acceptance test it threatens, e.g. REQ-005 or AT-008).

Pay special attention to:
1. Correctness of the search/filter SQL (case-insensitivity, SQL injection safety, composition of search+filter).
2. Whether PATCH update semantics correctly distinguish "field omitted" from "field explicitly cleared" (backend/app/crud.py, backend/app/schemas.py).
3. Whether the 404 paths are actually reachable for get/patch/delete on a nonexistent id.
4. Frontend accessibility: are all interactive controls actually reachable by accessible name/label, not just visually labeled?
5. Whether the loading/empty/error states in TaskList.tsx and useTasks.ts have any race conditions (e.g., stale responses from a superseded search overwriting fresher results).

7. Whether the CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and Playwright config (frontend/playwright.config.ts) actually wire the backend venv path and ports consistently — a subtle wiring mismatch here would make e2e silently unable to run in CI.
8. Any place where an /docs claim in README.md doesn't match what the code actually does.

Report your findings as a plain list, ordered Critical first, then Important, then Minor. If you find nothing at a given severity, say so explicitly (e.g., "No Critical findings"). Do not fix anything — this is a review only, report back what you found.

1	# DEFINE: TaskFlow
2	
3	> A locally runnable FastAPI + SQLite + React/TypeScript task manager with full CRUD, search, filter, and status workflow, validated inputs, and a restart-durable SQLite store.
4	
5	## Metadata
6	
7	| Attribute | Value |
8	|-----------|-------|
9	| **Feature** | TASKFLOW |
10	| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |
11	| **Author** | define-agent |
12	| **Status** | ✅ Complete (Designed) |
13	| **Clarity Score** | 14/15 |
14	
15	---
16	
17	## Problem Statement
18	
19	A single local user has no dependable, restart-durable way to create, organize, and track small tasks through a `todo → doing → done` workflow with search and filtering, without standing up authentication, multi-user infrastructure, or an external database.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Target Users
24	
25	| User | Role | Pain Point |
26	|------|------|------------|
27	| Single local user / developer | Runs the app on their own machine for personal task tracking | Needs a fast, dependable task list that survives restarts, works on any screen size, and gives clear feedback (loading/empty/error) — without needing an account, a server, or external infrastructure |
28	
29	---
30	
31	## Goals
32	
33	What success looks like (prioritized):
34	
35	| ID | Priority | Goal |
36	|----|----------|------|
37	| REQ-001 | **MUST** | Create, list, edit, and delete tasks via a JSON HTTP API |
38	| REQ-002 | **MUST** | Task status is one of `todo`/`doing`/`done` (default `todo`); a task can be moved between statuses |
39	| REQ-003 | **MUST** | Enforce field validation: title required after trim, 1–120 chars; description optional, ≤500 chars; status restricted to the three valid values |
40	| REQ-004 | **MUST** | Task data persists in SQLite and survives an application restart |
41	| REQ-005 | **MUST** | Search matches title and description, case-insensitively |
42	| REQ-006 | **MUST** | Filtering by status returns only tasks with the requested status |
43	| REQ-007 | **MUST** | Frontend works at desktop and mobile widths, performs all operations without page reloads, labels every interactive control accessibly, and visually distinguishes all three statuses |
44	| REQ-008 | **MUST** | Frontend exposes loading, empty, validation-error, and request-failure states |
45	| REQ-009 | **MUST** | Invalid input is rejected (whitespace-only title, title >120 chars, description >500 chars, unknown status) and a request for a missing task returns a not-found response |
46	| REQ-010 | **MUST** | Document supported runtime versions and exact clean install/run/test/lint/type-check/build commands |
47	| REQ-011 | **MUST** | Backend unit + integration tests, frontend component tests, and one browser end-to-end flow all exist and pass |
48	| REQ-012 | **MUST** | A CI workflow runs the documented checks (install, lint, type-check, test, build) on the feature branch |
49	| REQ-013 | **MUST** | Work lands on a feature branch with coherent commits, a clean working tree, and a root-level `PR.md` (title, summary, test evidence, risks, known limitations) |
50	
51	> Requirement IDs are stable for the feature's whole life (Define → Design task manifest → Traceability Matrix → Build → PR). Never renumbered on iteration; appended only.
52	
53	**Priority Guide:**
54	- **MUST** = MVP fails without this
55	- **SHOULD** = Important, but workaround exists
56	- **COULD** = Nice-to-have, cut first if needed
57	
58	All thirteen goals are MUST: the governing brief states every one of them as a hard requirement or explicit invalid-input rule, and none has a documented workaround — there is no SHOULD/COULD tier for this feature (confirmed during Brainstorm's YAGNI pass, which is where every deferrable feature — auth, drag-and-drop, tags, pagination, etc. — was already removed from scope).
59	
60	---
61	
62	## Success Criteria
63	
64	Measurable outcomes:
65	
66	- [ ] 100% of the seven required operations (create, list, edit, delete, search, filter, move-status) are implemented and each has at least one passing automated test
67	- [ ] 0 of the 4 documented invalid-input cases (whitespace-only title, title >120 chars, description >500 chars, unknown status) are accepted by the API — each returns a 4xx with no row written
68	- [ ] A request for a non-existent task id returns a not-found (404) response in 100% of cases
69	- [ ] A dataset created before a backend process restart is present, unchanged, and fully queryable after the restart (0 data loss)
70	- [ ] Search and status-filter queries return exactly the matching subset (0 false positives/negatives) across at least the boundary cases: empty query, case-mismatched query, and each of the 3 status values
71	- [ ] The frontend renders correctly and remains operable at both a desktop width (e.g. 1280px) and a mobile width (e.g. 375px)
72	- [ ] All 4 required UI states (loading, empty, validation error, request failure) are reachable and visually distinct
73	- [ ] `install`, `run`, `test`, `lint`, `type-check`, and `build` each succeed as a single documented command for both backend and frontend
74	- [ ] CI runs all documented checks and passes on the feature branch
75	
76	---
77	
78	## Acceptance Tests
79	
80	| ID | Scenario | Given | When | Then |
81	|----|----------|-------|------|------|
82	| AT-001 | Create a task (happy path) | No prior state needed | User submits a title of 1–120 trimmed chars (description optional) | A task is created with `status=todo`, a stable id, and `created_at`/`updated_at` timestamps; it appears in the list |
83	| AT-002 | Reject whitespace-only title | — | User submits a title of only spaces/tabs | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
84	| AT-003 | Reject title over 120 chars | — | User submits a 121-character title | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
85	| AT-004 | Reject description over 500 chars | — | User submits a 501-character description | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
86	| AT-005 | Reject unknown status | — | User submits `status="archived"` (or any value outside todo/doing/done) | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
87	| AT-006 | Not-found on missing task | A task id that does not exist in the store | User requests, edits, or deletes that id | API returns a 404 (not-found) response |
88	| AT-007 | Move a task between statuses | A task exists with `status=todo` | User edits the task's status to `doing`, then to `done` | The task's status updates each time; `updated_at` changes; the task appears under the correct status filter after each move |
89	| AT-008 | Case-insensitive search | Tasks exist titled "Buy Milk" and "Read Book" | User searches for `"MILK"` | Only "Buy Milk" is returned |
90	| AT-009 | Status filter isolation | Tasks exist in all three statuses | User filters by `status=doing` | Only `doing` tasks are returned; `todo` and `done` tasks are excluded |
91	| AT-010 | Restart persistence | At least one task has been created | The backend process is stopped and restarted | The previously created task(s) are still present and unchanged via `GET` |
92	| AT-011 | Frontend empty state | No tasks exist (or a search/filter matches none) | User loads the app or applies a non-matching search/filter | An accessible empty-state message is shown instead of a blank list or error |
93	| AT-012 | Frontend request-failure state | The backend is unreachable or returns a 5xx | User performs any operation | An accessible error/failure state is shown instead of a silent failure or crash |
94	
95	---
96	
97	## Out of Scope
98	
99	Explicitly NOT included in this feature:
100	
101	- Authentication, user accounts, or any multi-user/shared-ownership behavior
102	- Deployment configuration, containerization, or hosting of any kind
103	- Any external database engine (Postgres, MySQL, etc.) — SQLite only
104	- Drag-and-drop Kanban board interaction (status changes via a labeled control instead)
105	- Tags/labels, priorities, due dates, bulk operations, pagination, real-time sync (WebSockets/polling), dark mode/theming
106	- Inspecting or copying application code or planning artifacts from any other implementation or repository
107	
108	---
109	
110	## Constraints
111	
112	| Type | Constraint | Impact |
113	|------|------------|--------|
114	| Technical | Backend must be Python + FastAPI + SQLite; frontend must be React + TypeScript; API must be JSON over HTTP | Fixes the technology stack outright; Design phase selects concrete libraries within these bounds (ORM, build tool, test frameworks) |
115	| Technical | No authentication, multi-user behavior, deployment, or external database | Removes entire categories of design surface (auth middleware, session storage, infra-as-code, connection pooling to a networked DB) |
116	| Process | Must not inspect the other benchmark implementation or copy code/artifacts from outside this repository | Every file in this build must be authored fresh, grounded only in this repository's own context and this DEFINE document |
117	| Process | Must not create or publish a GitHub repository or pull request | `PR.md` is the deliverable, not an actual GitHub PR; no `gh pr create` or repo creation at any point |
118	| Environment | The `.claude/` directory tree is write-protected in this environment | SDD artifacts are kept at repo-root `sdd/` instead of `.claude/sdd/` (see Brainstorm decision log) |
119	| Timeline | No explicit deadline stated in the governing brief | Scope is bounded by completeness against the brief rather than a date; YAGNI keeps effort proportionate |
120	
121	---
122	
123	## Technical Context
124	
125	> Essential context for Design phase — prevents misplaced files and missed infrastructure needs.
126	
127	| Aspect | Value | Notes |
128	|--------|-------|-------|
129	| **Deployment Location** | Repo root, split into `backend/` (FastAPI + SQLite) and `frontend/` (React + TypeScript + Vite) | Clean separation; each half owns its own dependency manifest, test runner, and lint/type-check config |
130	| **KB Domains** | None applicable | The plugin KB (`kb/_index.yaml`) covers data-engineering domains only (dbt, Spark, Airflow, lakehouse, streaming); no web-application/FastAPI/React domain exists. Design will proceed on general framework-standard practice rather than a cited KB pattern (confidence 0.70, per Brainstorm) |
131	| **IaC Impact** | None | Deployment and infrastructure are explicitly out of scope |
132	
133	**Why This Matters:**
134	
135	- **Location** → Design phase uses correct project structure, prevents misplaced files
136	- **KB Domains** → No domain-specific patterns to pull; Design instead follows current FastAPI/React ecosystem conventions (SQLAlchemy 2.0, Pydantic v2, Vite, Vitest/RTL, Playwright) as selected in Brainstorm's Approach A
137	- **IaC Impact** → Confirmed none needed; avoids over-building infrastructure this feature doesn't require
138	
139	---
140	
141	## Data Contract
142	
143	Not applicable — this feature is a single-table CRUD application (`tasks`), not a data pipeline, ETL process, or analytics workload. No source systems, freshness SLAs, or lineage requirements apply.
144	
145	---
146	
147	## Risk Profile
148	
149	```yaml
150	risk_profile:
151	  level: low
152	  reasons:
153	    - "Single local process, single local user, no network exposure beyond localhost — blast_radius is low"
154	    - "No authentication/authorization surface exists to regress (explicitly out of scope) — security dimension stays low given ORM-parameterized queries (Brainstorm Approach A) rather than hand-built SQL"
155	    - "No destructive migration: schema is created once via ORM metadata, no existing data to migrate"
156	    - "SQLite file is local and git-ignored; worst case is loss of the user's own local task list, recoverable by recreating tasks — data_loss is low, not high, because there is no shared or production data at stake"
157	    - "All changes are reversible via git; no irreversible external side effects"
158	  dimensions:
159	    data_loss: low
160	    security: low
161	    reversibility: low
162	    blast_radius: low
163	    migration: none
164	  override:
165	    applied: false
166	    author: null
167	    rationale: null
168	```
169	
170	---
171	
172	## Assumptions
173	
174	Assumptions that if wrong could invalidate the design:
175	
176	| ID | Assumption | If Wrong, Impact | Validated? |
177	|----|------------|------------------|------------|
178	| A-001 | Exactly one process accesses the SQLite file at a time (single local user, no concurrent multi-process writers) | SQLite's file-level locking could cause `database is locked` errors under concurrent writes; would need a connection-pooling/queueing strategy | [x] — directly guaranteed by the brief's "no multi-user behavior" constraint |
179	| A-002 | Task volume stays in the hundreds, not millions, of rows | Would need pagination, indexing beyond the primary key, or virtualization on the frontend list | [ ] — reasonable for a single local user's personal task list, but not explicitly stated in the brief |
180	| A-003 | The user runs a current evergreen browser (Vite's default modern JS target) | Would need a broader Babel/polyfill transpilation target for legacy browser support | [ ] — reasonable default for a locally-run developer tool, not explicitly stated in the brief |
181	
182	**Note:** A-002 and A-003 are validated as reasonable defaults for this feature's stated context (single local developer tool) rather than confirmed by explicit statement in the brief; neither materially changes the architecture if wrong, since both have straightforward, additive fixes (pagination; broader build target) that don't require a redesign.
183	
184	---
185	
186	## Clarity Score Breakdown
187	
188	| Element | Score (0-3) | Notes |
189	|---------|-------------|-------|
190	| Problem | 3 | Single clear sentence, specific user, specific pain point (no durable/searchable/status-tracked task list without extra infra) |
191	| Users | 2 | One clearly identified persona with a concrete pain point; scored 2 rather than 3 because the feature has only a single user archetype to validate against (no secondary persona to cross-check design trade-offs) |
192	| Goals | 3 | 13 goals extracted directly from explicit brief statements, each assigned a stable REQ id and MoSCoW priority |
193	| Success | 3 | Every success criterion is stated as a countable/testable outcome (0 of N invalid cases accepted, 100% of operations tested, exact match on search/filter, etc.) |
194	| Scope | 3 | Out-of-scope list is explicit and directly sourced from the brief's exclusions plus Brainstorm's YAGNI pass |
195	| **Total** | **14/15** | |
196	
197	**Scoring Guide:**
198	- 0 = Missing entirely
199	- 1 = Vague or incomplete
200	- 2 = Clear but missing details
201	- 3 = Crystal clear, actionable
202	
203	**Minimum to proceed: 12/15** — ✅ 14/15 clears the gate.
204	
205	---
206	
207	## Open Questions
208	
209	None - ready for Design.
210	
211	---
212	
213	## Revision History
214	
215	| Version | Date | Author | Changes |
216	|---------|------|--------|---------|
217	| 1.0 | 2026-07-30 | define-agent | Initial version, derived from `sdd/features/BRAINSTORM_TASKFLOW.md` |
218	
219	---

222

content.content:
1	# DESIGN: TaskFlow
2	
3	> Technical design for implementing TaskFlow — a locally runnable FastAPI + SQLite + React/TypeScript task manager
4	
5	## Metadata
6	
7	| Attribute | Value |
8	|-----------|-------|
9	| **Feature** | TASKFLOW |
10	| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |
11	| **Author** | design-agent |
12	| **DEFINE** | [DEFINE_TASKFLOW.md](./DEFINE_TASKFLOW.md) |
13	| **Risk Level** | low — echoed from DEFINE: single local process/user, no auth surface, ORM-parameterized queries, no destructive migration, git-ignored SQLite file, all changes reversible via git |
14	| **Status** | Ready for Build |
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Architecture Overview
19	
20	```text
21	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
22	│                              SYSTEM DIAGRAM                                │
23	├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
24	│                                                                             │
25	│   ┌─────────────────────────┐        JSON/HTTP        ┌─────────────────┐ │
26	│   │   Browser (desktop or   │  ───────────────────►   │   FastAPI app   │ │
27	│   │   mobile viewport)      │   GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE │   (uvicorn)     │ │
28	│   │                         │  ◄───────────────────   │                 │ │
29	│   │  React + TypeScript SPA │        JSON responses   │  APIRouter:     │ │
30	│   │  ┌───────────────────┐  │                          │  /tasks         │ │
31	│   │  │ SearchFilterBar   │  │                          │  /tasks/{id}    │ │
32	│   │  │ TaskForm          │  │                          └────────┬────────┘ │
33	│   │  │ TaskList/TaskItem │  │                                   │          │
34	│   │  │ Loading/Empty/    │  │                          Pydantic v2 schemas │
35	│   │  │ Error states      │  │                          (validate in/out)   │
36	│   │  └───────────────────┘  │                                   │          │
37	│   └─────────────────────────┘                          SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM  │
38	│                                                                   │          │
39	│                                                                   ▼          │
40	│                                                          ┌─────────────────┐ │
41	│                                                          │  SQLite file    │ │
42	│                                                          │  backend/data/  │ │
43	│                                                          │  taskflow.db    │ │
44	│                                                          │  (persists      │ │
45	│                                                          │   across        │ │
46	│                                                          │   restarts)     │ │
47	│                                                          └─────────────────┘ │
48	└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
49	```
50	
51	---
52	
53	## Components
54	
55	| Component | Purpose | Technology |
56	|-----------|---------|------------|
57	| FastAPI app (`backend/app/main.py`) | HTTP entry point, CORS for the local Vite dev server, startup schema creation | Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Uvicorn |
58	| Task router (`backend/app/routers/tasks.py`) | REST endpoints: list (with search/filter), create, get, update, delete | FastAPI `APIRouter`, dependency-injected DB session |
59	| Schemas (`backend/app/schemas.py`) | Request/response validation: trim + length limits on title/description, status enum, timestamp serialization | Pydantic v2 |
60	| Models + DB session (`backend/app/models.py`, `backend/app/database.py`) | `Task` ORM mapping to the `tasks` table; SQLite engine/session factory | SQLAlchemy 2.0 (declarative + `Session`) |
61	| CRUD layer (`backend/app/crud.py`) | Query construction: case-insensitive search (`LIKE` on lowered columns), status filter, create/update/delete logic, `updated_at` bump | SQLAlchemy Core expressions |
62	| React SPA (`frontend/src/`) | Single page: search/filter bar, task list, create/edit form, per-task status control, loading/empty/validation/error states | React 18, TypeScript, Vite |
63	| API client (`frontend/src/api/client.ts`) | Typed `fetch` wrapper: builds query strings, parses JSON, normalizes error shapes | TypeScript, native `fetch` |
64	| Backend test suite (`backend/tests/`) | Unit tests (schema validation) + integration tests (full API via `TestClient`, temp SQLite file) | pytest, `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` |
65	| Frontend test suite (`frontend/src/**/*.test.tsx`) | Component tests: rendering, form validation feedback, state transitions, accessibility roles | Vitest, React Testing Library |
66	| E2E suite (`frontend/e2e/`) | One full browser flow: create → search → filter → move status → delete, against the real backend | Playwright |
67	| CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) | Runs install/lint/type-check/test/build for both halves on every push/PR | GitHub Actions |
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Key Decisions
72	
73	### Decision 1: SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM + Pydantic v2 for persistence and validation
74	
75	| Attribute | Value |
76	|-----------|-------|
77	| **Status** | Accepted |
78	| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |
79	
80	**Context:** The backend must persist tasks in SQLite and enforce exact field constraints (title 1–120 trimmed, description ≤500, status enum) with no external database and no KB pattern to draw from (confirmed in Brainstorm: no FastAPI/React domain in this plugin's KB).
81	
82	**Choice:** Use SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative models as the single source of schema truth, with Pydantic v2 `BaseModel` schemas (`TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskRead`) for request/response validation, wired through FastAPI's `response_model` and dependency-injected sessions.
83	
84	**Rationale:** SQLAlchemy guarantees parameterized queries (no hand-built SQL to audit for injection); Pydantic v2's `Field(min_length=1, max_length=120)` plus a `field_validator` for trimming maps directly onto the brief's exact numeric constraints and produces structured 422 error bodies the frontend can render as validation state.
85	
86	**Alternatives Rejected:**
87	1. Raw `sqlite3` + hand-written SQL — rejected because every query becomes a manual injection-audit surface with no compile-time schema guarantee (Brainstorm Approach B).
88	2. SQLModel — rejected as an unnecessary extra abstraction layer for a single-table schema; SQLAlchemy directly is more mature and no less code here (Brainstorm Approach C, partial).
89	
90	**Consequences:**
91	- Trade-off: one more dependency (`sqlalchemy`) beyond the stdlib.
92	- Benefit: schema, validation, and query safety all come from well-tested, idiomatic libraries rather than custom code that must be independently verified in review.
93	
94	---
95	
96	### Decision 2: Status changes via `PATCH /tasks/{id}`, not a dedicated transition endpoint
97	
98	| Attribute | Value |
99	|-----------|-------|
100	| **Status** | Accepted |
101	| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |
102	
103	**Context:** The brief requires the ability to move a task between `todo`/`doing`/`done` alongside ordinary field edits (title, description).
104	
105	**Choice:** Expose a single `PATCH /tasks/{id}` endpoint accepting any subset of `{title, description, status}`; moving a task is just a `PATCH` with `{"status": "doing"}`.
106	
107	**Rationale:** The brief describes status change as one of several editable attributes, not a distinct workflow with transition guards, history, or side effects. A single partial-update endpoint covers every "edit" requirement (REQ-001) and the "move" requirement (REQ-002) with one code path to validate and test.
108	
109	**Alternatives Rejected:**
110	1. Separate `POST /tasks/{id}/move` endpoint — rejected: adds a second code path and a second set of tests for behavior that is identical to a field edit once validation passes.
111	
112	**Consequences:**
113	- Trade-off: the API does not model status transitions as a guarded state machine (e.g., cannot forbid `done → todo` even if a future spec wanted that).
114	- Benefit: one endpoint, one validation path, fewer places for the 4 invalid-input rules to be enforced inconsistently.
115	
116	---
117	
118	### Decision 3: Search and filter as server-side query parameters on `GET /tasks`
119	
120	| Attribute | Value |
121	|-----------|-------|
122	| **Status** | Accepted |
123	| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |
124	
125	**Context:** Search must match title/description case-insensitively; filtering must return only the requested status; both must compose (a search within a status).
126	
127	**Choice:** `GET /tasks?q=<term>&status=<todo|doing|done>` — both optional, combinable, evaluated in SQLAlchemy as `WHERE lower(title) LIKE lower(:q) OR lower(description) LIKE lower(:q)` (when `q` given) `AND status = :status` (when `status` given).
128	
129	**Rationale:** Server-side filtering keeps one source of truth for "what matches" and lets the frontend show a correct loading state per request rather than fetching the whole table and filtering client-side (which also breaks the loading/empty-state model REQ-008 requires per query).
130	
131	**Alternatives Rejected:**
132	1. Fetch all tasks once, filter/search in the browser — rejected: cannot produce a real per-query loading state, and silently stops matching correctly if the dataset grows beyond a single fetch's practical size (see DEFINE assumption A-002).
133	
134	**Consequences:**
135	- Trade-off: every search keystroke (once debounced) is a network round trip.
136	- Benefit: filtering logic exists in exactly one place, and is exactly what the backend integration tests exercise.
137	
138	---
139	
140	### Decision 4: SQLite file path and schema creation lifecycle
141	
142	| Attribute | Value |
143	|-----------|-------|
144	| **Status** | Accepted |
145	| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |
146	
147	**Context:** Data must survive a restart of the application; the repo must stay clean of environment-specific binary artifacts.
148	
149	**Choice:** SQLite file lives at `backend/data/taskflow.db` (path overridable via a `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` environment variable for tests); the directory is created on startup if missing; `Base.metadata.create_all(engine)` runs once at FastAPI startup (idempotent — safe to run every restart).
150	
151	**Rationale:** A fixed on-disk path with `create_all` at startup satisfies "survive a restart" with zero migration tooling, matching Brainstorm Decision 1 (no Alembic — the schema is fixed for this build). Tests override `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` to a temp file so they never touch the real data file.
152	
153	**Alternatives Rejected:**
154	1. In-memory SQLite (`:memory:`) as the default — rejected outright: fails the restart-persistence requirement (REQ-004) by definition.
155	
156	**Consequences:**
157	- Trade-off: the DB file must be `.gitignore`d, or every run's data would appear in git status.
158	- Benefit: zero-configuration persistence; `rm backend/data/taskflow.db` is the entire "reset" procedure if ever needed manually.
159	
160	---
161	
162	## File Manifest

505	### Pattern 1: FastAPI router + Pydantic schema + SQLAlchemy session (backend)
506	
507	```python
508	# backend/app/routers/tasks.py — representative shape, not full implementation
509	from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
510	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
511	
512	from app.database import get_db
513	from app.schemas import TaskCreate, TaskRead, TaskUpdate
514	from app import crud
515	
516	router = APIRouter(prefix="/tasks", tags=["tasks"])
517	
518	
519	@router.get("", response_model=list[TaskRead])
520	def list_tasks(q: str | None = None, status: str | None = None, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
521	    return crud.list_tasks(db, search=q, status=status)
522	
523	
524	@router.post("", response_model=TaskRead, status_code=201)
525	def create_task(payload: TaskCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
526	    return crud.create_task(db, payload)
527	
528	
529	@router.patch("/{task_id}", response_model=TaskRead)
530	def update_task(task_id: str, payload: TaskUpdate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
531	    task = crud.update_task(db, task_id, payload)
532	    if task is None:
533	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Task not found")
534	    return task
535	```
536	
537	### Pattern 2: Pydantic v2 validation (trim + length + enum)
538	
539	```python
540	# backend/app/schemas.py — representative shape, not full implementation
541	from datetime import datetime
542	from enum import Enum
543	
544	from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator
545	
546	
547	class TaskStatus(str, Enum):
548	    todo = "todo"
549	    doing = "doing"
550	    done = "done"
551	
552	
553	class TaskCreate(BaseModel):
554	    title: str
555	    description: str | None = None
556	    status: TaskStatus = TaskStatus.todo
557	
558	    @field_validator("title")
559	    @classmethod
560	    def title_must_be_nonblank_and_bounded(cls, v: str) -> str:
561	        trimmed = v.strip()
562	        if not (1 <= len(trimmed) <= 120):
563	            raise ValueError("title must be 1-120 characters after trimming")
564	        return trimmed
565	
566	    @field_validator("description")
567	    @classmethod
568	    def description_bounded(cls, v: str | None) -> str | None:
569	        if v is not None and len(v) > 500:
570	            raise ValueError("description must be at most 500 characters")
571	        return v
572	```
573	
574	### Pattern 3: React data-fetching hook (frontend)
575	
576	```typescript
577	// frontend/src/hooks/useTasks.ts — representative shape, not full implementation
578	import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
579	import { listTasks } from "../api/client";
580	import type { Task, TaskStatus, ApiError } from "../types";
581	
582	export function useTasks(query: string, status: TaskStatus | "all") {
583	  const [tasks, setTasks] = useState<Task[] | null>(null);
584	  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
585	  const [error, setError] = useState<ApiError | null>(null);
586	
587	  const refetch = useCallback(async () => {
588	    setLoading(true);
589	    setError(null);
590	    try {
591	      const result = await listTasks({ q: query || undefined, status: status === "all" ? undefined : status });
592	      setTasks(result);
593	    } catch (err) {
594	      setError(err as ApiError);
595	    } finally {
596	      setLoading(false);
597	    }
598	  }, [query, status]);
599	
600	  useEffect(() => {
601	    refetch();
602	  }, [refetch]);
603	
604	  return { tasks, loading, error, refetch };
605	}
606	```
607	
608	---
609	
610	## Data Flow
611	
612	```text
613	1. User types in SearchFilterBar or submits TaskForm / changes a TaskItem's status select
614	   │
615	   ▼
616	2. App.tsx / useTasks calls the typed API client (frontend/src/api/client.ts),
617	   which builds a query string / JSON body and issues fetch()
618	   │
619	   ▼
620	3. FastAPI router (backend/app/routers/tasks.py) receives the request;
621	   Pydantic validates the payload (schemas.py) — invalid input returns 422 here,
622	   before any DB access
623	   │
624	   ▼
625	4. crud.py builds a SQLAlchemy query/statement against the Task model
626	   and executes it through the session from database.py
627	   │
628	   ▼
629	5. SQLite file (backend/data/taskflow.db) is read/written; the row(s) affected
630	   are returned as ORM objects
631	   │
632	   ▼
633	6. FastAPI serializes the ORM objects via the TaskRead response_model back to JSON
634	   │
635	   ▼
636	7. The frontend hook updates {tasks, loading, error} state; components re-render
637	   the list, or the form shows the validation error, or an error banner appears
638	   on network/5xx failure — all without a page reload
639	```
640	
641	---
642	
643	## Integration Points
644	
645	| External System | Integration Type | Authentication |
646	|-----------------|-----------------|----------------|
647	| None | — | — |
648	
649	No external systems are integrated — the only "integration" is the frontend SPA calling its own co-located FastAPI backend over local HTTP, which is the core architecture itself rather than an external dependency. This is intentional per the DEFINE's constraints (no auth, no external DB, no deployment).
650	
651	---
652	
653	## Testing Strategy
654	
655	| Test Type | Scope | Files | Tools | Coverage Goal |
656	|-----------|-------|-------|-------|---------------|
657	| Unit | Pydantic schema validation boundaries (title/description/status) | `backend/tests/test_schemas.py` | pytest | Every boundary in DEFINE AT-002–AT-005 |
658	| Integration | Full API behavior against a real (temp-file) SQLite DB | `backend/tests/test_tasks_api.py` | pytest + `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` | Every acceptance test AT-001, AT-006–AT-010 |
659	| Component | Frontend rendering, validation feedback, state transitions, accessible queries | `frontend/src/components/*.test.tsx` | Vitest + React Testing Library | AT-002–AT-005 (validation UI), AT-011, AT-012 (empty/failure states) |
660	| E2E | One full browser journey: create → search → filter → move status → delete | `frontend/e2e/taskflow.spec.ts` | Playwright | AT-001, AT-007, AT-008, AT-009 combined in one flow |
661	
662	The strategy covers every acceptance test in the DEFINE (AT-001 through AT-012): AT-001/006/007/008/009/010 map to backend integration tests; AT-002–005 map to backend unit tests (rejection) and frontend component tests (validation-state rendering); AT-011/AT-012 map to frontend component tests for the empty and request-failure states; the Playwright flow exercises AT-001, AT-007, AT-008, AT-009 together as a real user journey.
663	
664	---
665	
666	## Error Handling
667	
668	| Error Type | Handling Strategy | Retry? |
669	|------------|-------------------|--------|
670	| Pydantic validation failure (bad title/description/status) | FastAPI returns 422 with a structured error body; frontend renders it as an inline validation-error state on the form | No |
671	| Task id not found (GET/PATCH/DELETE) | Router raises `HTTPException(404)`; frontend shows a not-found message for that action | No |
672	| Network failure / backend unreachable / 5xx | API client catches the fetch rejection or non-2xx status and returns a typed `ApiError`; frontend shows a top-level request-failure banner with a retry action | Yes — user-triggered retry via the same `refetch()` |
673	| Unexpected server exception | FastAPI's default 500 handler returns a generic JSON error; treated identically to the network-failure case on the frontend (no internal detail leaked) | No |
674	
675	---
676	
677	## Configuration
678	
679	| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
680	|------------|------|---------|--------------|
681	| `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` | string (env var) | `backend/data/taskflow.db` | SQLite file path; overridden to a temp path in tests |
682	| `TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` | string (env var, comma-separated) | `http://localhost:5173` | Origins allowed to call the API (the local Vite dev server) |
683	| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | string (frontend env var) | `http://localhost:8000` | Base URL the frontend API client targets |
684	
685	---
686	
687	## Security Considerations
688	
689	- No authentication/authorization is implemented — explicitly out of scope; the app is intended for a single local user on their own machine only, never exposed beyond `localhost`.
690	- All SQL is generated via SQLAlchemy's parameterized query construction — no string-formatted SQL anywhere, eliminating SQL injection risk (Decision 1).
691	- Pydantic validates and rejects malformed/oversized input before it reaches the database layer, bounding request-body size implicitly via the 120/500-character field limits.
692	- CORS is restricted to the known local dev origin via `TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` rather than left wide open (`*`).
693	- The SQLite file is `.gitignore`d so no local task data is ever committed to version control.
694	
695	---
696	
697	## Observability
698	
699	| Aspect | Implementation |
700	|--------|----------------|
701	| Logging | FastAPI/Uvicorn's default structured access + error logging to stdout; no additional logging infrastructure needed for a local single-user tool |
702	| Metrics | None — out of scope; no operational metrics pipeline exists or is needed for a locally run tool with no deployment target |
703	| Tracing | None — out of scope for the same reason |
704	
705	---
706	
707	## Pipeline Architecture
708	
709	Not applicable — TaskFlow is a single-table CRUD application, not a data pipeline, ETL process, or analytics workload. No DAG, partitioning, incremental strategy, or data-quality-gate sections apply.

8	def list_tasks(db: Session, search: str | None = None, status: str | None = None) -> list[Task]:
9	    stmt = select(Task)
10	    if search:
11	        pattern = f"%{search.lower()}%"
12	        stmt = stmt.where(
13	            or_(
14	                func.lower(Task.title).like(pattern),
15	                func.lower(func.coalesce(Task.description, "")).like(pattern),
16	            )
17	        )
18	    if status:
19	        stmt = stmt.where(Task.status == status)
20	    stmt = stmt.order_by(Task.created_at.desc())
21	    return list(db.execute(stmt).scalars().all())
22	
23	
24	def get_task(db: Session, task_id: str) -> Task | None:
25	    return db.get(Task, task_id)

28	def create_task(db: Session, payload: TaskCreate) -> Task:
29	    task = Task(
30	        title=payload.title,
31	        description=payload.description,
32	        status=payload.status.value,
33	    )
34	    db.add(task)
35	    db.commit()
36	    db.refresh(task)
37	    return task

40	def update_task(db: Session, task_id: str, payload: TaskUpdate) -> Task | None:
41	    task = get_task(db, task_id)
42	    if task is None:
43	        return None
44	    updates = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
45	    for field, value in updates.items():
46	        if field == "status" and value is not None:
47	            value = value.value if hasattr(value, "value") else value
48	        setattr(task, field, value)
49	    db.add(task)
50	    db.commit()
51	    db.refresh(task)
52	    return task

1	# TaskFlow
2	
3	A locally runnable, full-stack task manager: create, list, edit, delete, search, and filter
4	tasks, and move them between `todo`, `doing`, and `done`. Backend is Python/FastAPI/SQLite;
5	frontend is React/TypeScript. No authentication, no multi-user behavior, no deployment, no
6	external database — this is a single-user, local tool.
7	
8	## Runtime versions
9	
10	Tested with:
11	
12	| Tool | Version |
13	|------|---------|
14	| Python | 3.13.7 (any 3.11+ works; CI pins 3.13) |
15	| Node.js | v25.5.0 (CI pins 25; requires >=22.22.2 for the frontend's test tooling) |
16	| npm | 11.8.0 |
17	
18	Check yours with `python3 --version`, `node --version`, `npm --version`.
19	
20	## Project layout
21	
22	```text
23	backend/    FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + SQLite API (Python)
24	frontend/   React + TypeScript SPA (Vite), component tests, and the Playwright e2e suite
25	```
26	
27	Each half is independent: its own dependency manifest, its own test runner, its own
28	lint/type-check/build commands. There is no shared code between them — they communicate only
29	over HTTP/JSON.
30	
31	---
32	
33	## Backend — `backend/`
34	
35	### Clean install
36	
37	```bash
38	cd backend
39	python3 -m venv .venv
40	source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
41	python -m pip install --upgrade pip
42	pip install -e ".[dev]"
43	```
44	
45	### Run
46	
47	```bash
48	cd backend
49	source .venv/bin/activate
50	uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
51	```
52	
53	The API is now at `http://localhost:8000` (interactive docs at `/docs`). The SQLite file is
54	created on first run at `backend/data/taskflow.db` and persists across restarts. Override its
55	location with the `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` environment variable; override allowed CORS origins with
56	`TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` (comma-separated, defaults to the Vite dev server's origin).
57	
58	### Test
59	
60	```bash
61	cd backend
62	source .venv/bin/activate
63	python -m pytest -q
64	```
65	
66	40 tests: unit tests for Pydantic validation boundaries (`tests/test_schemas.py`) and
67	integration tests against the real API + a temp SQLite file, including a restart-persistence
68	test (`tests/test_tasks_api.py`).
69	
70	### Lint
71	
72	```bash
73	cd backend
74	source .venv/bin/activate
75	ruff check .
76	```
77	
78	### Type-check
79	
80	```bash
81	cd backend
82	source .venv/bin/activate
83	mypy app
84	```
85	
86	(`mypy` runs in `strict` mode against `app/`; test files are covered by `pytest`'s own
87	type-annotated style but are not part of the strict gate.)
88	
89	### Build
90	
91	The backend has no separate build step — `uvicorn app.main:app` runs it directly from source,
92	which is the deployable unit for a locally run tool.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## Frontend — `frontend/`
97	
98	### Clean install
99	
100	```bash
101	cd frontend
102	npm install
103	```
104	
105	(`npm ci` also works once `package-lock.json` exists, and is what CI uses for a byte-for-byte
106	reproducible install.)
107	
108	### Run
109	
110	```bash
111	cd frontend
112	npm run dev
113	```
114	
115	Opens the dev server at `http://localhost:5173`. In dev mode, API calls to `/api/*` are
116	proxied to `http://localhost:8000` (see `vite.config.ts`) — run the backend first.
117	
118	### Test
119	
120	```bash
121	cd frontend
122	npm run test:run
123	```
124	
125	25 component tests (Vitest + React Testing Library) covering form validation, list
126	loading/empty/error states, search/filter behavior, status changes, edit, and delete, across
127	`SearchFilterBar`, `TaskForm`, `TaskList`, and `App`.
128	
129	### Lint
130	
131	```bash
132	cd frontend
133	npm run lint
134	```
135	
136	### Type-check
137	
138	```bash
139	cd frontend
140	npm run typecheck
141	```
142	
143	### Build
144	
145	```bash
146	cd frontend
147	npm run build
148	```
149	
150	Produces a production bundle in `frontend/dist/`. Preview it with `npm run preview` (serves on
151	`http://localhost:4173`).
152	
153	### End-to-end test (Playwright)
154	
155	Requires the backend's virtualenv to already exist at `backend/.venv` (run the backend clean
156	install above first) and Playwright's browser binaries:
157	
158	```bash
159	cd frontend
160	npx playwright install --with-deps chromium   # one-time
161	npm run e2e
162	```
163	
164	This spins up the real backend (on an isolated `backend/data/e2e-test.db`) and a production
165	frontend build (`vite preview` on port 4173), then runs one full browser flow
166	(`e2e/taskflow.spec.ts`): create a task, search for it, filter by status, move it
167	`todo → doing → done`, filter by its new status, then delete it.
168	
169	---
170	
171	## CI
172	
173	`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every push and pull request, as three jobs:
174	
175	1. **backend** — `pip install -e ".[dev]"`, `ruff check .`, `mypy app`, `python -m pytest -q`
176	2. **frontend** — `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:run`, `npm run build`
177	3. **e2e** — installs both halves, installs Playwright's Chromium, runs `npx playwright test`
178	
179	All three must pass for the workflow to succeed.
180	
181	## API summary
182	
183	| Method | Path | Purpose |
184	|--------|------|---------|
185	| `GET` | `/tasks?q=&status=` | List tasks; `q` searches title+description case-insensitively, `status` filters to one of `todo`/`doing`/`done`; both optional and combinable |
186	| `POST` | `/tasks` | Create a task (`title` required, `description` optional, `status` optional, defaults to `todo`) |
187	| `GET` | `/tasks/{id}` | Get one task; 404 if it doesn't exist |
188	| `PATCH` | `/tasks/{id}` | Partially update a task (title, description, and/or status — this is also how a task is moved between statuses); 404 if it doesn't exist |
189	| `DELETE` | `/tasks/{id}` | Delete a task; 404 if it doesn't exist |
190	
191	Validation (enforced server-side, returns `422` on failure): `title` must be 1–120 characters
192	after trimming whitespace; `description` must be at most 500 characters; `status` must be one
193	of `todo`, `doing`, `done`.
194	
195	## Configuration reference
196	
197	| Variable | Where | Default | Purpose |
198	|----------|-------|---------|---------|
199	| `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` | backend | `backend/data/taskflow.db` | SQLite file location |
200	| `TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` | backend | `http://localhost:5173,http://127.0.0.1:5173` | Allowed CORS origins (comma-separated) |
201	| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | frontend | `/api` (dev proxy) | Base URL the frontend's API client targets; set to the backend's real origin for `preview`/e2e |
202	
203	## Documentation and planning artifacts
204	
205	The full brainstorm → requirements → design → build record for this feature lives under
206	[`sdd/features/`](./sdd/features/) and [`sdd/reports/`](./sdd/reports/) (kept at the repo root
207	because `.claude/sdd/` was not writable in the environment this was built in — see the
208	Brainstorm document's Key Decisions for detail).

summary:
## Code Review Report — TaskFlow (feature/taskflow-remediation)

Reviewed the full diff since `06a4117` (backend FastAPI/SQLAlchemy/SQLite app, frontend React/TS app, tests, CI, Playwright, docs) against `sdd/features/DEFINE_TASKFLOW.md` and `sdd/features/DESIGN_TASKFLOW.md`. All backend tests (40), ruff, mypy --strict, frontend typecheck/lint/vitest (25 tests), and `vite build` were actually executed and pass. I also reproduced two concrete bugs below via direct `TestClient` calls rather than just reading code.

---

### CRITICAL

**[C1] `PATCH /tasks/{id}` crashes with an unhandled 500 instead of a 422 when `title` or `status` is explicitly set to `null`.**

# TaskFlow

A locally runnable, full-stack task manager: create, list, edit, delete, search, and filter
tasks, and move them between `todo`, `doing`, and `done`. Backend is Python/FastAPI/SQLite;
frontend is React/TypeScript. No authentication, no multi-user behavior, no deployment, no
external database — this is a single-user, local tool.

## Runtime versions

Tested with:

| Tool | Version |
|------|---------|
| Python | 3.13.7 (any 3.11+ works; CI pins 3.13) |
| Node.js | v25.5.0 (CI pins 25; requires >=22.22.2 for the frontend's test tooling) |
| npm | 11.8.0 |

Check yours with `python3 --version`, `node --version`, `npm --version`.

## Project layout

```text
backend/    FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + SQLite API (Python)
frontend/   React + TypeScript SPA (Vite), component tests, and the Playwright e2e suite
```

Each half is independent: its own dependency manifest, its own test runner, its own
lint/type-check/build commands. There is no shared code between them — they communicate only
over HTTP/JSON.

---

## Backend — `backend/`

### Clean install

```bash
cd backend
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

### Run

```bash
cd backend
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

The API is now at `http://localhost:8000` (interactive docs at `/docs`). The SQLite file is
created on first run at `backend/data/taskflow.db` and persists across restarts. Override its
location with the `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` environment variable; override allowed CORS origins with
`TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` (comma-separated, defaults to the Vite dev server's origin).

### Test

```bash
cd backend
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pytest -q
```

40 tests: unit tests for Pydantic validation boundaries (`tests/test_schemas.py`) and
integration tests against the real API + a temp SQLite file, including a restart-persistence
test (`tests/test_tasks_api.py`).

### Lint

```bash
cd backend
source .venv/bin/activate
ruff check .
```

### Type-check

```bash
cd backend
source .venv/bin/activate
mypy app
```

(`mypy` runs in `strict` mode against `app/`; test files are covered by `pytest`'s own
type-annotated style but are not part of the strict gate.)

### Build

The backend has no separate build step — `uvicorn app.main:app` runs it directly from source,
which is the deployable unit for a locally run tool.

---

## Frontend — `frontend/`

### Clean install

```bash
cd frontend
npm install
```

(`npm ci` also works once `package-lock.json` exists, and is what CI uses for a byte-for-byte
reproducible install.)

### Run

```bash
cd frontend
npm run dev
```

Opens the dev server at `http://localhost:5173`. In dev mode, API calls to `/api/*` are
proxied to `http://localhost:8000` (see `vite.config.ts`) — run the backend first.

### Test

```bash
cd frontend
npm run test:run
```

25 component tests (Vitest + React Testing Library) covering form validation, list
loading/empty/error states, search/filter behavior, status changes, edit, and delete, across
`SearchFilterBar`, `TaskForm`, `TaskList`, and `App`.

### Lint

```bash
cd frontend
npm run lint
```

### Type-check

```bash
cd frontend
npm run typecheck
```

### Build

```bash
cd frontend
npm run build
```

Produces a production bundle in `frontend/dist/`. Preview it with `npm run preview` (serves on
`http://localhost:4173`).

### End-to-end test (Playwright)

Requires the backend's virtualenv to already exist at `backend/.venv` (run the backend clean
install above first) and Playwright's browser binaries:

```bash
cd frontend
npx playwright install --with-deps chromium   # one-time
npm run e2e
```

This spins up the real backend (on an isolated `backend/data/e2e-test.db`) and a production
frontend build (`vite preview` on port 4173), then runs one full browser flow
(`e2e/taskflow.spec.ts`): create a task, search for it, filter by status, move it
`todo → doing → done`, filter by its new status, then delete it.

---

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every push and pull request, as three jobs:

1. **backend** — `pip install -e ".[dev]"`, `ruff check .`, `mypy app`, `python -m pytest -q`
2. **frontend** — `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:run`, `npm run build`
3. **e2e** — installs both halves, installs Playwright's Chromium, runs `npx playwright test`

All three must pass for the workflow to succeed.

## API summary

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| `GET` | `/tasks?q=&status=` | List tasks; `q` searches title+description case-insensitively, `status` filters to one of `todo`/`doing`/`done`; both optional and combinable |
| `POST` | `/tasks` | Create a task (`title` required, `description` optional, `status` optional, defaults to `todo`) |
| `GET` | `/tasks/{id}` | Get one task; 404 if it doesn't exist |
| `PATCH` | `/tasks/{id}` | Partially update a task (title, description, and/or status — this is also how a task is moved between statuses); 404 if it doesn't exist |
| `DELETE` | `/tasks/{id}` | Delete a task; 404 if it doesn't exist |

Validation (enforced server-side, returns `422` on failure): `title` must be 1–120 characters
after trimming whitespace; `description` must be at most 500 characters; `status` must be one
of `todo`, `doing`, `done`.

## Configuration reference

| Variable | Where | Default | Purpose |
|----------|-------|---------|---------|
| `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` | backend | `backend/data/taskflow.db` | SQLite file location |
| `TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` | backend | `http://localhost:5173,http://127.0.0.1:5173` | Allowed CORS origins (comma-separated) |
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | frontend | `/api` (dev proxy) | Base URL the frontend's API client targets; set to the backend's real origin for `preview`/e2e |

## Documentation and planning artifacts

The full brainstorm → requirements → design → build record for this feature lives under
[`sdd/features/`](./sdd/features/) and [`sdd/reports/`](./sdd/reports/) (kept at the repo root
because `.claude/sdd/` was not writable in the environment this was built in — see the
Brainstorm document's Key Decisions for detail).

+_LIKE_ESCAPE_CHAR = "\\"
+
+

+    # Escape the LIKE wildcards themselves so a literal "%" or "_" in a
+    # search term is matched literally instead of matching anything/one-char.

## Code Review Report — Round 2 (Scoped Re-Review)

**Reviewer:** code-reviewer
**Files reviewed:** `backend/app/schemas.py`, `backend/app/crud.py`, `backend/tests/test_schemas.py`, `backend/tests/test_tasks_api.py`, `frontend/src/components/TaskItem.tsx`, `frontend/src/App.test.tsx`, `frontend/e2e/taskflow.spec.ts`, `README.md`, plus `backend/app/routers/tasks.py`, `backend/app/models.py`, `backend/app/config.py`, `backend/app/main.py` for cross-checking context.
**Verification method:** read every changed line plus surrounding context; empirically ran the actual `TaskUpdate` model and `_escape_like_term` in the project's own `.venv` (not the test suite) to confirm Pydantic v2 `exclude_unset`/`validate_default` semantics and LIKE-escaping order, rather than trusting test names.

### Summary of prior findings

| ID | Status | Reason |
|----|--------|--------|
| C1 | **RESOLVED** | `validate_title`/`validate_status` field_validators now raise `ValueError` when `None` is received, and since `TaskUpdate` is a FastAPI request-body model, the raised `ValidationError` is converted by FastAPI into a 422 automatically — never reaches `crud.update_task`/the DB, so the IntegrityError path is unreachable. |
| I1 | **RESOLVED** | `_escape_like_term` escapes the backslash character *before* escaping `%`/`_`, which is the correct order (escaping backslash after would double-escape the newly inserted escape characters); both the title and description `.like()` calls consistently pass `escape=_LIKE_ESCAPE_CHAR`. |
| I2 | **RESOLVED** | Appending `(${shortId})` to every visible label/button text makes each control's rendered text (and therefore its accessible name, since there's no separate `aria-label`) unique, and it still contains the human-readable title, so WCAG 2.5.3 Label-in-Name is preserved. |
| I3 | **RESOLVED** | `test_patch_explicit_null_description_clears_it` exercises a real PATCH through the API (not just the Pydantic model) and asserts `200` + `description is None`, genuinely covering the one field where explicit-null clearing must succeed. |
| M1 | **RESOLVED** | README now states the literal two-origin default (`http://localhost:5173,http://127.0.0.1:5173`), which matches `config.py`'s `get_cors_origins()` default exactly. |

### Detailed verification notes

**C1 — Pydantic v2 semantics (verified empirically, not assumed):**
```
case1 omitted status -> title='New title' ... {'title'}          # partial update still works
case2 explicit status -> status=<TaskStatus.doing> ... {'status'} # explicit valid value passes
case3 explicit null status -> ValidationError                    # explicit null rejected
case4 explicit null title  -> ValidationError                    # explicit null rejected
case5 empty body -> {} unset                                     # no-op works
```
This confirms the code comment's claim is correct: Pydantic v2 field_validators do not run when a field is *omitted* (default `None` is used untouched, `validate_default=False` by default), but they do run for any explicitly-supplied value, including an explicit `null`. So the fix rejects explicit `null` for `title`/`status` without breaking normal partial updates that simply don't mention those keys (this is also independently exercised by the pre-existing, unmodified tests `test_edit_title_and_description` and `test_move_task_through_full_status_workflow`, which patch a subset of fields and were already green).

**I1 — LIKE escaping (verified empirically):**
```
_escape_like_term('100% off')            -> '100\% off'
_escape_like_term('a_b')                 -> 'a\_b'
_escape_like_term('back\\slash')  (1 \)  -> 'back\\slash' (2 \)   # backslash doubled correctly
_escape_like_term('50%_done\\\\') (2 \)  -> '50\%\_done\\\\\\\\' (4 \)
```
Order is backslash-first, then `%`, then `_` — correct. Both `.like(pattern, escape=_LIKE_ESCAPE_CHAR)` calls (title and description-coalesce clauses) use the same escape character, so there's no asymmetry between the two OR branches.

**I2 — Accessible name uniqueness:** `shortId = task.id.slice(0, 8)` is derived from `uuid.uuid4().hex` (32 hex chars, backend `models.py`), giving 32 bits of entropy per prefix — practically unique for realistic task volumes in this app (not cryptographically guaranteed, but not a concern for a todo-list app; noted below as a minor observation only).

**Test quality check:** The new frontend test `"gives duplicate-titled tasks distinct accessible control names"` uses two mock tasks whose IDs differ in their first 8 hex characters and asserts both `getByRole("button", {name: ...})` queries succeed independently — this is a real assertion of uniqueness (if the suffixes collided, one of the two `getByRole` calls would throw "unable to find element"), not a false positive. The backend `test_search_escapes_like_wildcards` test uses `%` and `_` search terms against titles that do/don't contain those literal characters and checks exact match sets — correctly distinguishes the escaped-vs-unescaped behavior, not a coincidental pass.

### New findings from this diff

No Critical or Important new issues found.

- **[Minor]** `frontend/src/components/TaskItem.tsx:78,94,100,108` — The `(${shortId})` suffix is rendered as *visible* text to end users (not just exposed via `aria-label`), so every task card now visibly shows a raw 8-character hex ID fragment next to each button/label. This satisfies the accessibility requirement but is a minor UX/cosmetic trade-off worth a product decision (e.g., could instead be a visually-hidden `<span className="sr-only">` suffix to keep the accessible name unique without cluttering the visible UI). Not a bug, no fix required unless the team wants a cleaner visual.
- **[Minor]** `frontend/src/components/TaskItem.tsx:26` — `shortId` uniqueness is probabilistic (8 hex chars ≈ 32 bits), not guaranteed; a very large task list could theoretically produce two IDs sharing the same 8-char prefix. Practically negligible for this app's scale, informational only.

No new findings in `backend/app/schemas.py`, `backend/app/crud.py`, or `README.md`.

## Code Review Report — Round 2 (Scoped Re-Review)

**Reviewer:** code-reviewer
**Files reviewed:** `backend/app/schemas.py`, `backend/app/crud.py`, `backend/tests/test_schemas.py`, `backend/tests/test_tasks_api.py`, `frontend/src/components/TaskItem.tsx`, `frontend/src/App.test.tsx`, `frontend/e2e/taskflow.spec.ts`, `README.md`, plus `backend/app/routers/tasks.py`, `backend/app/models.py`, `backend/app/config.py`, `backend/app/main.py` for cross-checking context.
**Verification method:** read every changed line plus surrounding context; empirically ran the actual `TaskUpdate` model and `_escape_like_term` in the project's own `.venv` (not the test suite) to confirm Pydantic v2 `exclude_unset`/`validate_default` semantics and LIKE-escaping order, rather than trusting test names.

### Summary of prior findings

| ID | Status | Reason |
|----|--------|--------|
| C1 | **RESOLVED** | `validate_title`/`validate_status` field_validators now raise `ValueError` when `None` is received, and since `TaskUpdate` is a FastAPI request-body model, the raised `ValidationError` is converted by FastAPI into a 422 automatically — never reaches `crud.update_task`/the DB, so the IntegrityError path is unreachable. |
| I1 | **RESOLVED** | `_escape_like_term` escapes the backslash character *before* escaping `%`/`_`, which is the correct order (escaping backslash after would double-escape the newly inserted escape characters); both the title and description `.like()` calls consistently pass `escape=_LIKE_ESCAPE_CHAR`. |
| I2 | **RESOLVED** | Appending `(${shortId})` to every visible label/button text makes each control's rendered text (and therefore its accessible name, since there's no separate `aria-label`) unique, and it still contains the human-readable title, so WCAG 2.5.3 Label-in-Name is preserved. |
| I3 | **RESOLVED** | `test_patch_explicit_null_description_clears_it` exercises a real PATCH through the API (not just the Pydantic model) and asserts `200` + `description is None`, genuinely covering the one field where explicit-null clearing must succeed. |
| M1 | **RESOLVED** | README now states the literal two-origin default (`http://localhost:5173,http://127.0.0.1:5173`), which matches `config.py`'s `get_cors_origins()` default exactly. |

### Detailed verification notes

**C1 — Pydantic v2 semantics (verified empirically, not assumed):**
```
case1 omitted status -> title='New title' ... {'title'}          # partial update still works
case2 explicit status -> status=<TaskStatus.doing> ... {'status'} # explicit valid value passes
case3 explicit null status -> ValidationError                    # explicit null rejected
case4 explicit null title  -> ValidationError                    # explicit null rejected
case5 empty body -> {} unset                                     # no-op works
```
This confirms the code comment's claim is correct: Pydantic v2 field_validators do not run when a field is *omitted* (default `None` is used untouched, `validate_default=False` by default), but they do run for any explicitly-supplied value, including an explicit `null`. So the fix rejects explicit `null` for `title`/`status` without breaking normal partial updates that simply don't mention those keys (this is also independently exercised by the pre-existing, unmodified tests `test_edit_title_and_description` and `test_move_task_through_full_status_workflow`, which patch a subset of fields and were already green).

**I1 — LIKE escaping (verified empirically):**
```
_escape_like_term('100% off')            -> '100\% off'
_escape_like_term('a_b')                 -> 'a\_b'
_escape_like_term('back\\slash')  (1 \)  -> 'back\\slash' (2 \)   # backslash doubled correctly
_escape_like_term('50%_done\\\\') (2 \)  -> '50\%\_done\\\\\\\\' (4 \)
```
Order is backslash-first, then `%`, then `_` — correct. Both `.like(pattern, escape=_LIKE_ESCAPE_CHAR)` calls (title and description-coalesce clauses) use the same escape character, so there's no asymmetry between the two OR branches.

**I2 — Accessible name uniqueness:** `shortId = task.id.slice(0, 8)` is derived from `uuid.uuid4().hex` (32 hex chars, backend `models.py`), giving 32 bits of entropy per prefix — practically unique for realistic task volumes in this app (not cryptographically guaranteed, but not a concern for a todo-list app; noted below as a minor observation only).

**Test quality check:** The new frontend test `"gives duplicate-titled tasks distinct accessible control names"` uses two mock tasks whose IDs differ in their first 8 hex characters and asserts both `getByRole("button", {name: ...})` queries succeed independently — this is a real assertion of uniqueness (if the suffixes collided, one of the two `getByRole` calls would throw "unable to find element"), not a false positive. The backend `test_search_escapes_like_wildcards` test uses `%` and `_` search terms against titles that do/don't contain those literal characters and checks exact match sets — correctly distinguishes the escaped-vs-unescaped behavior, not a coincidental pass.

### New findings from this diff

No Critical or Important new issues found.

- **[Minor]** `frontend/src/components/TaskItem.tsx:78,94,100,108` — The `(${shortId})` suffix is rendered as *visible* text to end users (not just exposed via `aria-label`), so every task card now visibly shows a raw 8-character hex ID fragment next to each button/label. This satisfies the accessibility requirement but is a minor UX/cosmetic trade-off worth a product decision (e.g., could instead be a visually-hidden `<span className="sr-only">` suffix to keep the accessible name unique without cluttering the visible UI). Not a bug, no fix required unless the team wants a cleaner visual.
- **[Minor]** `frontend/src/components/TaskItem.tsx:26` — `shortId` uniqueness is probabilistic (8 hex chars ≈ 32 bits), not guaranteed; a very large task list could theoretically produce two IDs sharing the same 8-char prefix. Practically negligible for this app's scale, informational only.

## Autonomous Decisions

| # | Decision Point | Options Considered | Chose | Rationale |
|---|----------------|--------------------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | `.claude/sdd/` write-protected — where to put SDD artifacts | (a) keep retrying `.claude/sdd/`, (b) redirect to repo-root `sdd/`, (c) skip artifact persistence | (b) repo-root `sdd/` | Preserves the full brainstorm→define→design→build→ship record the brief explicitly requires, without depending on a permission the environment won't grant; documented as a Key Decision rather than silently deviating |
| 2 | Commit granularity — per-Task-Manifest-task commits vs. per-phase-group commits | (a) one commit per manifest task (12 commits), (b) group related tasks into one coherent commit per logical unit (scaffold+CRUD together, tests together, etc.) | (b) grouped commits | Building directly (no Task-tool delegation per task) made task-by-task commit granularity impractical without artificial splitting of a single coherent code change; grouped commits still give a clean, reviewable history (11 commits, each independently buildable) — this is the `commit_parallel` contract's sanctioned "impractical granularity → session, with justification" fallback |
| 3 | Runtime tooling versions — pin older, previously-audited majors vs. current majors | (a) ESLint 8 / Vite 5 / Vitest 2 (initially planned in DESIGN), (b) current majors (ESLint 10 flat config, Vite 8, Vitest 4, TypeScript 5.9) | (b) current majors | `npm audit` showed 14 vulnerabilities (1 critical) against the initially-planned versions, 0 against current majors; "production-quality" per the brief favors the audited-clean option even though it required rewriting the ESLint config to flat format |
| 4 | PATCH null-handling for `title`/`status` (surfaced by the review, not pre-decided in DESIGN) | (a) silently ignore an explicit `null` (treat as omitted), (b) reject explicit `null` with a 422, (c) allow clearing and store an empty string instead | (b) reject with 422 | Matches the DEFINE's own constraint that title/status are always required (never legitimately empty); silently ignoring (a) would surprise API consumers, and storing an empty string (c) would violate REQ-003's non-negotiable title-required rule |
| 5 | Accessible-name disambiguation for duplicate-titled tasks (surfaced by the review) | (a) visible short-id suffix on every control's label/text, (b) `aria-label` override that duplicates title differently from visible text, (c) enforce title uniqueness in the backend | (a) visible short-id suffix | (b) risks a WCAG 2.5.3 Label-in-Name violation (accessible name diverging from visible text); (c) would add a uniqueness constraint the DEFINE never asked for and that real task lists reasonably violate (e.g., two "Follow up" tasks); (a) is the smallest correct fix, accepted with a minor cosmetic trade-off recorded in Known Limitations |

## Autonomous Decisions

| # | Decision Point | Options Considered | Chose | Rationale |
|---|----------------|--------------------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | `.claude/sdd/` write-protected — where to put SDD artifacts | (a) keep retrying `.claude/sdd/`, (b) redirect to repo-root `sdd/`, (c) skip artifact persistence | (b) repo-root `sdd/` | Preserves the full brainstorm→define→design→build→ship record the brief explicitly requires, without depending on a permission the environment won't grant; documented as a Key Decision rather than silently deviating |
| 2 | Commit granularity — per-Task-Manifest-task commits vs. per-phase-group commits | (a) one commit per manifest task (12 commits), (b) group related tasks into one coherent commit per logical unit (scaffold+CRUD together, tests together, etc.) | (b) grouped commits | Building directly (no Task-tool delegation per task) made task-by-task commit granularity impractical without artificial splitting of a single coherent code change; grouped commits still give a clean, reviewable history (11 commits, each independently buildable) — this is the `commit_parallel` contract's sanctioned "impractical granularity → session, with justification" fallback |
| 3 | Runtime tooling versions — pin older, previously-audited majors vs. current majors | (a) ESLint 8 / Vite 5 / Vitest 2 (initially planned in DESIGN), (b) current majors (ESLint 10 flat config, Vite 8, Vitest 4, TypeScript 5.9) | (b) current majors | `npm audit` showed 14 vulnerabilities (1 critical) against the initially-planned versions, 0 against current majors; "production-quality" per the brief favors the audited-clean option even though it required rewriting the ESLint config to flat format |
| 4 | PATCH null-handling for `title`/`status` (surfaced by the review, not pre-decided in DESIGN) | (a) silently ignore an explicit `null` (treat as omitted), (b) reject explicit `null` with a 422, (c) allow clearing and store an empty string instead | (b) reject with 422 | Matches the DEFINE's own constraint that title/status are always required (never legitimately empty); silently ignoring (a) would surprise API consumers, and storing an empty string (c) would violate REQ-003's non-negotiable title-required rule |
| 5 | Accessible-name disambiguation for duplicate-titled tasks (surfaced by the review) | (a) visible short-id suffix on every control's label/text, (b) `aria-label` override that duplicates title differently from visible text, (c) enforce title uniqueness in the backend | (a) visible short-id suffix | (b) risks a WCAG 2.5.3 Label-in-Name violation (accessible name diverging from visible text); (c) would add a uniqueness constraint the DEFINE never asked for and that real task lists reasonably violate (e.g., two "Follow up" tasks); (a) is the smallest correct fix, accepted with a minor cosmetic trade-off recorded in Known Limitations |

## Autonomous Decisions

| # | Decision Point | Options Considered | Chose | Rationale |
|---|----------------|--------------------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | `.claude/sdd/` write-protected — where to put SDD artifacts | (a) keep retrying `.claude/sdd/`, (b) redirect to repo-root `sdd/`, (c) skip artifact persistence | (b) repo-root `sdd/` | Preserves the full brainstorm→define→design→build→ship record the brief explicitly requires, without depending on a permission the environment won't grant; documented as a Key Decision rather than silently deviating |
| 2 | Commit granularity — per-Task-Manifest-task commits vs. per-phase-group commits | (a) one commit per manifest task (12 commits), (b) group related tasks into one coherent commit per logical unit (scaffold+CRUD together, tests together, etc.) | (b) grouped commits | Building directly (no Task-tool delegation per task) made task-by-task commit granularity impractical without artificial splitting of a single coherent code change; grouped commits still give a clean, reviewable history (11 commits, each independently buildable) — this is the `commit_parallel` contract's sanctioned "impractical granularity → session, with justification" fallback |
| 3 | Runtime tooling versions — pin older, previously-audited majors vs. current majors | (a) ESLint 8 / Vite 5 / Vitest 2 (initially planned in DESIGN), (b) current majors (ESLint 10 flat config, Vite 8, Vitest 4, TypeScript 5.9) | (b) current majors | `npm audit` showed 14 vulnerabilities (1 critical) against the initially-planned versions, 0 against current majors; "production-quality" per the brief favors the audited-clean option even though it required rewriting the ESLint config to flat format |
| 4 | PATCH null-handling for `title`/`status` (surfaced by the review, not pre-decided in DESIGN) | (a) silently ignore an explicit `null` (treat as omitted), (b) reject explicit `null` with a 422, (c) allow clearing and store an empty string instead | (b) reject with 422 | Matches the DEFINE's own constraint that title/status are always required (never legitimately empty); silently ignoring (a) would surprise API consumers, and storing an empty string (c) would violate REQ-003's non-negotiable title-required rule |
| 5 | Accessible-name disambiguation for duplicate-titled tasks (surfaced by the review) | (a) visible short-id suffix on every control's label/text, (b) `aria-label` override that duplicates title differently from visible text, (c) enforce title uniqueness in the backend | (a) visible short-id suffix | (b) risks a WCAG 2.5.3 Label-in-Name violation (accessible name diverging from visible text); (c) would add a uniqueness constraint the DEFINE never asked for and that real task lists reasonably violate (e.g., two "Follow up" tasks); (a) is the smallest correct fix, accepted with a minor cosmetic trade-off recorded in Known Limitations |
