## Autonomous Decisions

| # | Decision Point | Options Considered | Chose | Rationale |
|---|----------------|--------------------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | `.claude/sdd/` write-protected — where to put SDD artifacts | (a) keep retrying `.claude/sdd/`, (b) redirect to repo-root `sdd/`, (c) skip artifact persistence | (b) repo-root `sdd/` | Preserves the full brainstorm→define→design→build→ship record the brief explicitly requires, without depending on a permission the environment won't grant; documented as a Key Decision rather than silently deviating |
| 2 | Commit granularity — per-Task-Manifest-task commits vs. per-phase-group commits | (a) one commit per manifest task (12 commits), (b) group related tasks into one coherent commit per logical unit (scaffold+CRUD together, tests together, etc.) | (b) grouped commits | Building directly (no Task-tool delegation per task) made task-by-task commit granularity impractical without artificial splitting of a single coherent code change; grouped commits still give a clean, reviewable history (11 commits, each independently buildable) — this is the `commit_parallel` contract's sanctioned "impractical granularity → session, with justification" fallback |
| 3 | Runtime tooling versions — pin older, previously-audited majors vs. current majors | (a) ESLint 8 / Vite 5 / Vitest 2 (initially planned in DESIGN), (b) current majors (ESLint 10 flat config, Vite 8, Vitest 4, TypeScript 5.9) | (b) current majors | `npm audit` showed 14 vulnerabilities (1 critical) against the initially-planned versions, 0 against current majors; "production-quality" per the brief favors the audited-clean option even though it required rewriting the ESLint config to flat format |
| 4 | PATCH null-handling for `title`/`status` (surfaced by the review, not pre-decided in DESIGN) | (a) silently ignore an explicit `null` (treat as omitted), (b) reject explicit `null` with a 422, (c) allow clearing and store an empty string instead | (b) reject with 422 | Matches the DEFINE's own constraint that title/status are always required (never legitimately empty); silently ignoring (a) would surprise API consumers, and storing an empty string (c) would violate REQ-003's non-negotiable title-required rule |
| 5 | Accessible-name disambiguation for duplicate-titled tasks (surfaced by the review) | (a) visible short-id suffix on every control's label/text, (b) `aria-label` override that duplicates title differently from visible text, (c) enforce title uniqueness in the backend | (a) visible short-id suffix | (b) risks a WCAG 2.5.3 Label-in-Name violation (accessible name diverging from visible text); (c) would add a uniqueness constraint the DEFINE never asked for and that real task lists reasonably violate (e.g., two "Follow up" tasks); (a) is the smallest correct fix, accepted with a minor cosmetic trade-off recorded in Known Limitations |

## Autonomous Decisions

| # | Decision Point | Options Considered | Chose | Rationale |
|---|----------------|--------------------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | `.claude/sdd/` write-protected — where to put SDD artifacts | (a) keep retrying `.claude/sdd/`, (b) redirect to repo-root `sdd/`, (c) skip artifact persistence | (b) repo-root `sdd/` | Preserves the full brainstorm→define→design→build→ship record the brief explicitly requires, without depending on a permission the environment won't grant; documented as a Key Decision rather than silently deviating |
| 2 | Commit granularity — per-Task-Manifest-task commits vs. per-phase-group commits | (a) one commit per manifest task (12 commits), (b) group related tasks into one coherent commit per logical unit (scaffold+CRUD together, tests together, etc.) | (b) grouped commits | Building directly (no Task-tool delegation per task) made task-by-task commit granularity impractical without artificial splitting of a single coherent code change; grouped commits still give a clean, reviewable history (11 commits, each independently buildable) — this is the `commit_parallel` contract's sanctioned "impractical granularity → session, with justification" fallback |
| 3 | Runtime tooling versions — pin older, previously-audited majors vs. current majors | (a) ESLint 8 / Vite 5 / Vitest 2 (initially planned in DESIGN), (b) current majors (ESLint 10 flat config, Vite 8, Vitest 4, TypeScript 5.9) | (b) current majors | `npm audit` showed 14 vulnerabilities (1 critical) against the initially-planned versions, 0 against current majors; "production-quality" per the brief favors the audited-clean option even though it required rewriting the ESLint config to flat format |
| 4 | PATCH null-handling for `title`/`status` (surfaced by the review, not pre-decided in DESIGN) | (a) silently ignore an explicit `null` (treat as omitted), (b) reject explicit `null` with a 422, (c) allow clearing and store an empty string instead | (b) reject with 422 | Matches the DEFINE's own constraint that title/status are always required (never legitimately empty); silently ignoring (a) would surprise API consumers, and storing an empty string (c) would violate REQ-003's non-negotiable title-required rule |
| 5 | Accessible-name disambiguation for duplicate-titled tasks (surfaced by the review) | (a) visible short-id suffix on every control's label/text, (b) `aria-label` override that duplicates title differently from visible text, (c) enforce title uniqueness in the backend | (a) visible short-id suffix | (b) risks a WCAG 2.5.3 Label-in-Name violation (accessible name diverging from visible text); (c) would add a uniqueness constraint the DEFINE never asked for and that real task lists reasonably violate (e.g., two "Follow up" tasks); (a) is the smallest correct fix, accepted with a minor cosmetic trade-off recorded in Known Limitations |

# DEFINE: TaskFlow

> A locally runnable FastAPI + SQLite + React/TypeScript task manager with full CRUD, search, filter, and status workflow, validated inputs, and a restart-durable SQLite store.

## Metadata

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Feature** | TASKFLOW |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |
| **Author** | define-agent |
| **Status** | ✅ Complete (Designed) |
| **Clarity Score** | 14/15 |

---

## Problem Statement

A single local user has no dependable, restart-durable way to create, organize, and track small tasks through a `todo → doing → done` workflow with search and filtering, without standing up authentication, multi-user infrastructure, or an external database.

---

## Target Users

| User | Role | Pain Point |
|------|------|------------|
| Single local user / developer | Runs the app on their own machine for personal task tracking | Needs a fast, dependable task list that survives restarts, works on any screen size, and gives clear feedback (loading/empty/error) — without needing an account, a server, or external infrastructure |

---

## Goals

What success looks like (prioritized):

| ID | Priority | Goal |
|----|----------|------|
| REQ-001 | **MUST** | Create, list, edit, and delete tasks via a JSON HTTP API |
| REQ-002 | **MUST** | Task status is one of `todo`/`doing`/`done` (default `todo`); a task can be moved between statuses |
| REQ-003 | **MUST** | Enforce field validation: title required after trim, 1–120 chars; description optional, ≤500 chars; status restricted to the three valid values |
| REQ-004 | **MUST** | Task data persists in SQLite and survives an application restart |
| REQ-005 | **MUST** | Search matches title and description, case-insensitively |
| REQ-006 | **MUST** | Filtering by status returns only tasks with the requested status |
| REQ-007 | **MUST** | Frontend works at desktop and mobile widths, performs all operations without page reloads, labels every interactive control accessibly, and visually distinguishes all three statuses |
| REQ-008 | **MUST** | Frontend exposes loading, empty, validation-error, and request-failure states |
| REQ-009 | **MUST** | Invalid input is rejected (whitespace-only title, title >120 chars, description >500 chars, unknown status) and a request for a missing task returns a not-found response |
| REQ-010 | **MUST** | Document supported runtime versions and exact clean install/run/test/lint/type-check/build commands |
| REQ-011 | **MUST** | Backend unit + integration tests, frontend component tests, and one browser end-to-end flow all exist and pass |
| REQ-012 | **MUST** | A CI workflow runs the documented checks (install, lint, type-check, test, build) on the feature branch |
| REQ-013 | **MUST** | Work lands on a feature branch with coherent commits, a clean working tree, and a root-level `PR.md` (title, summary, test evidence, risks, known limitations) |

> Requirement IDs are stable for the feature's whole life (Define → Design task manifest → Traceability Matrix → Build → PR). Never renumbered on iteration; appended only.

**Priority Guide:**
- **MUST** = MVP fails without this
- **SHOULD** = Important, but workaround exists
- **COULD** = Nice-to-have, cut first if needed

All thirteen goals are MUST: the governing brief states every one of them as a hard requirement or explicit invalid-input rule, and none has a documented workaround — there is no SHOULD/COULD tier for this feature (confirmed during Brainstorm's YAGNI pass, which is where every deferrable feature — auth, drag-and-drop, tags, pagination, etc. — was already removed from scope).

---

## Success Criteria

Measurable outcomes:

- [ ] 100% of the seven required operations (create, list, edit, delete, search, filter, move-status) are implemented and each has at least one passing automated test
- [ ] 0 of the 4 documented invalid-input cases (whitespace-only title, title >120 chars, description >500 chars, unknown status) are accepted by the API — each returns a 4xx with no row written
- [ ] A request for a non-existent task id returns a not-found (404) response in 100% of cases
- [ ] A dataset created before a backend process restart is present, unchanged, and fully queryable after the restart (0 data loss)
- [ ] Search and status-filter queries return exactly the matching subset (0 false positives/negatives) across at least the boundary cases: empty query, case-mismatched query, and each of the 3 status values
- [ ] The frontend renders correctly and remains operable at both a desktop width (e.g. 1280px) and a mobile width (e.g. 375px)
- [ ] All 4 required UI states (loading, empty, validation error, request failure) are reachable and visually distinct
- [ ] `install`, `run`, `test`, `lint`, `type-check`, and `build` each succeed as a single documented command for both backend and frontend
- [ ] CI runs all documented checks and passes on the feature branch

---

## Acceptance Tests

| ID | Scenario | Given | When | Then |
|----|----------|-------|------|------|
| AT-001 | Create a task (happy path) | No prior state needed | User submits a title of 1–120 trimmed chars (description optional) | A task is created with `status=todo`, a stable id, and `created_at`/`updated_at` timestamps; it appears in the list |
| AT-002 | Reject whitespace-only title | — | User submits a title of only spaces/tabs | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
| AT-003 | Reject title over 120 chars | — | User submits a 121-character title | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
| AT-004 | Reject description over 500 chars | — | User submits a 501-character description | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
| AT-005 | Reject unknown status | — | User submits `status="archived"` (or any value outside todo/doing/done) | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
| AT-006 | Not-found on missing task | A task id that does not exist in the store | User requests, edits, or deletes that id | API returns a 404 (not-found) response |
| AT-007 | Move a task between statuses | A task exists with `status=todo` | User edits the task's status to `doing`, then to `done` | The task's status updates each time; `updated_at` changes; the task appears under the correct status filter after each move |
| AT-008 | Case-insensitive search | Tasks exist titled "Buy Milk" and "Read Book" | User searches for `"MILK"` | Only "Buy Milk" is returned |
| AT-009 | Status filter isolation | Tasks exist in all three statuses | User filters by `status=doing` | Only `doing` tasks are returned; `todo` and `done` tasks are excluded |
| AT-010 | Restart persistence | At least one task has been created | The backend process is stopped and restarted | The previously created task(s) are still present and unchanged via `GET` |
| AT-011 | Frontend empty state | No tasks exist (or a search/filter matches none) | User loads the app or applies a non-matching search/filter | An accessible empty-state message is shown instead of a blank list or error |
| AT-012 | Frontend request-failure state | The backend is unreachable or returns a 5xx | User performs any operation | An accessible error/failure state is shown instead of a silent failure or crash |

---

## Out of Scope

Explicitly NOT included in this feature:

- Authentication, user accounts, or any multi-user/shared-ownership behavior
- Deployment configuration, containerization, or hosting of any kind
- Any external database engine (Postgres, MySQL, etc.) — SQLite only
- Drag-and-drop Kanban board interaction (status changes via a labeled control instead)
- Tags/labels, priorities, due dates, bulk operations, pagination, real-time sync (WebSockets/polling), dark mode/theming
- Inspecting or copying application code or planning artifacts from any other implementation or repository

---

## Constraints

| Type | Constraint | Impact |
|------|------------|--------|
| Technical | Backend must be Python + FastAPI + SQLite; frontend must be React + TypeScript; API must be JSON over HTTP | Fixes the technology stack outright; Design phase selects concrete libraries within these bounds (ORM, build tool, test frameworks) |
| Technical | No authentication, multi-user behavior, deployment, or external database | Removes entire categories of design surface (auth middleware, session storage, infra-as-code, connection pooling to a networked DB) |
| Process | Must not inspect the other benchmark implementation or copy code/artifacts from outside this repository | Every file in this build must be authored fresh, grounded only in this repository's own context and this DEFINE document |
| Process | Must not create or publish a GitHub repository or pull request | `PR.md` is the deliverable, not an actual GitHub PR; no `gh pr create` or repo creation at any point |
| Environment | The `.claude/` directory tree is write-protected in this environment | SDD artifacts are kept at repo-root `sdd/` instead of `.claude/sdd/` (see Brainstorm decision log) |
| Timeline | No explicit deadline stated in the governing brief | Scope is bounded by completeness against the brief rather than a date; YAGNI keeps effort proportionate |

---

## Technical Context

> Essential context for Design phase — prevents misplaced files and missed infrastructure needs.

| Aspect | Value | Notes |
|--------|-------|-------|
| **Deployment Location** | Repo root, split into `backend/` (FastAPI + SQLite) and `frontend/` (React + TypeScript + Vite) | Clean separation; each half owns its own dependency manifest, test runner, and lint/type-check config |
| **KB Domains** | None applicable | The plugin KB (`kb/_index.yaml`) covers data-engineering domains only (dbt, Spark, Airflow, lakehouse, streaming); no web-application/FastAPI/React domain exists. Design will proceed on general framework-standard practice rather than a cited KB pattern (confidence 0.70, per Brainstorm) |
| **IaC Impact** | None | Deployment and infrastructure are explicitly out of scope |

**Why This Matters:**

- **Location** → Design phase uses correct project structure, prevents misplaced files
- **KB Domains** → No domain-specific patterns to pull; Design instead follows current FastAPI/React ecosystem conventions (SQLAlchemy 2.0, Pydantic v2, Vite, Vitest/RTL, Playwright) as selected in Brainstorm's Approach A
- **IaC Impact** → Confirmed none needed; avoids over-building infrastructure this feature doesn't require

---

## Data Contract

Not applicable — this feature is a single-table CRUD application (`tasks`), not a data pipeline, ETL process, or analytics workload. No source systems, freshness SLAs, or lineage requirements apply.

---

## Assumptions

Assumptions that if wrong could invalidate the design:

| ID | Assumption | If Wrong, Impact | Validated? |
|----|------------|------------------|------------|
| A-001 | Exactly one process accesses the SQLite file at a time (single local user, no concurrent multi-process writers) | SQLite's file-level locking could cause `database is locked` errors under concurrent writes; would need a connection-pooling/queueing strategy | [x] — directly guaranteed by the brief's "no multi-user behavior" constraint |
| A-002 | Task volume stays in the hundreds, not millions, of rows | Would need pagination, indexing beyond the primary key, or virtualization on the frontend list | [ ] — reasonable for a single local user's personal task list, but not explicitly stated in the brief |
| A-003 | The user runs a current evergreen browser (Vite's default modern JS target) | Would need a broader Babel/polyfill transpilation target for legacy browser support | [ ] — reasonable default for a locally-run developer tool, not explicitly stated in the brief |

**Note:** A-002 and A-003 are validated as reasonable defaults for this feature's stated context (single local developer tool) rather than confirmed by explicit statement in the brief; neither materially changes the architecture if wrong, since both have straightforward, additive fixes (pagination; broader build target) that don't require a redesign.

# DESIGN: TaskFlow

> Technical design for implementing TaskFlow — a locally runnable FastAPI + SQLite + React/TypeScript task manager

## Metadata

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Feature** | TASKFLOW |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |
| **Author** | design-agent |
| **DEFINE** | [DEFINE_TASKFLOW.md](./DEFINE_TASKFLOW.md) |
| **Risk Level** | low — echoed from DEFINE: single local process/user, no auth surface, ORM-parameterized queries, no destructive migration, git-ignored SQLite file, all changes reversible via git |
| **Status** | Ready for Build |

---

## Architecture Overview

```text
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                              SYSTEM DIAGRAM                                │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│   ┌─────────────────────────┐        JSON/HTTP        ┌─────────────────┐ │
│   │   Browser (desktop or   │  ───────────────────►   │   FastAPI app   │ │
│   │   mobile viewport)      │   GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE │   (uvicorn)     │ │
│   │                         │  ◄───────────────────   │                 │ │
│   │  React + TypeScript SPA │        JSON responses   │  APIRouter:     │ │
│   │  ┌───────────────────┐  │                          │  /tasks         │ │
│   │  │ SearchFilterBar   │  │                          │  /tasks/{id}    │ │
│   │  │ TaskForm          │  │                          └────────┬────────┘ │
│   │  │ TaskList/TaskItem │  │                                   │          │
│   │  │ Loading/Empty/    │  │                          Pydantic v2 schemas │
│   │  │ Error states      │  │                          (validate in/out)   │
│   │  └───────────────────┘  │                                   │          │
│   └─────────────────────────┘                          SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM  │
│                                                                   │          │
│                                                                   ▼          │
│                                                          ┌─────────────────┐ │
│                                                          │  SQLite file    │ │
│                                                          │  backend/data/  │ │
│                                                          │  taskflow.db    │ │
│                                                          │  (persists      │ │
│                                                          │   across        │ │
│                                                          │   restarts)     │ │
│                                                          └─────────────────┘ │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Components

| Component | Purpose | Technology |
|-----------|---------|------------|
| FastAPI app (`backend/app/main.py`) | HTTP entry point, CORS for the local Vite dev server, startup schema creation | Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Uvicorn |
| Task router (`backend/app/routers/tasks.py`) | REST endpoints: list (with search/filter), create, get, update, delete | FastAPI `APIRouter`, dependency-injected DB session |
| Schemas (`backend/app/schemas.py`) | Request/response validation: trim + length limits on title/description, status enum, timestamp serialization | Pydantic v2 |
| Models + DB session (`backend/app/models.py`, `backend/app/database.py`) | `Task` ORM mapping to the `tasks` table; SQLite engine/session factory | SQLAlchemy 2.0 (declarative + `Session`) |
| CRUD layer (`backend/app/crud.py`) | Query construction: case-insensitive search (`LIKE` on lowered columns), status filter, create/update/delete logic, `updated_at` bump | SQLAlchemy Core expressions |
| React SPA (`frontend/src/`) | Single page: search/filter bar, task list, create/edit form, per-task status control, loading/empty/validation/error states | React 18, TypeScript, Vite |
| API client (`frontend/src/api/client.ts`) | Typed `fetch` wrapper: builds query strings, parses JSON, normalizes error shapes | TypeScript, native `fetch` |
| Backend test suite (`backend/tests/`) | Unit tests (schema validation) + integration tests (full API via `TestClient`, temp SQLite file) | pytest, `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` |
| Frontend test suite (`frontend/src/**/*.test.tsx`) | Component tests: rendering, form validation feedback, state transitions, accessibility roles | Vitest, React Testing Library |
| E2E suite (`frontend/e2e/`) | One full browser flow: create → search → filter → move status → delete, against the real backend | Playwright |
| CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) | Runs install/lint/type-check/test/build for both halves on every push/PR | GitHub Actions |

---

## Key Decisions

### Decision 1: SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM + Pydantic v2 for persistence and validation

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Status** | Accepted |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**Context:** The backend must persist tasks in SQLite and enforce exact field constraints (title 1–120 trimmed, description ≤500, status enum) with no external database and no KB pattern to draw from (confirmed in Brainstorm: no FastAPI/React domain in this plugin's KB).

**Choice:** Use SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative models as the single source of schema truth, with Pydantic v2 `BaseModel` schemas (`TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskRead`) for request/response validation, wired through FastAPI's `response_model` and dependency-injected sessions.

**Rationale:** SQLAlchemy guarantees parameterized queries (no hand-built SQL to audit for injection); Pydantic v2's `Field(min_length=1, max_length=120)` plus a `field_validator` for trimming maps directly onto the brief's exact numeric constraints and produces structured 422 error bodies the frontend can render as validation state.

**Alternatives Rejected:**
1. Raw `sqlite3` + hand-written SQL — rejected because every query becomes a manual injection-audit surface with no compile-time schema guarantee (Brainstorm Approach B).
2. SQLModel — rejected as an unnecessary extra abstraction layer for a single-table schema; SQLAlchemy directly is more mature and no less code here (Brainstorm Approach C, partial).

**Consequences:**
- Trade-off: one more dependency (`sqlalchemy`) beyond the stdlib.
- Benefit: schema, validation, and query safety all come from well-tested, idiomatic libraries rather than custom code that must be independently verified in review.

---

### Decision 2: Status changes via `PATCH /tasks/{id}`, not a dedicated transition endpoint

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Status** | Accepted |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**Context:** The brief requires the ability to move a task between `todo`/`doing`/`done` alongside ordinary field edits (title, description).

**Choice:** Expose a single `PATCH /tasks/{id}` endpoint accepting any subset of `{title, description, status}`; moving a task is just a `PATCH` with `{"status": "doing"}`.

**Rationale:** The brief describes status change as one of several editable attributes, not a distinct workflow with transition guards, history, or side effects. A single partial-update endpoint covers every "edit" requirement (REQ-001) and the "move" requirement (REQ-002) with one code path to validate and test.

**Alternatives Rejected:**
1. Separate `POST /tasks/{id}/move` endpoint — rejected: adds a second code path and a second set of tests for behavior that is identical to a field edit once validation passes.

**Consequences:**
- Trade-off: the API does not model status transitions as a guarded state machine (e.g., cannot forbid `done → todo` even if a future spec wanted that).
- Benefit: one endpoint, one validation path, fewer places for the 4 invalid-input rules to be enforced inconsistently.

---

### Decision 3: Search and filter as server-side query parameters on `GET /tasks`

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Status** | Accepted |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**Context:** Search must match title/description case-insensitively; filtering must return only the requested status; both must compose (a search within a status).

**Choice:** `GET /tasks?q=<term>&status=<todo|doing|done>` — both optional, combinable, evaluated in SQLAlchemy as `WHERE lower(title) LIKE lower(:q) OR lower(description) LIKE lower(:q)` (when `q` given) `AND status = :status` (when `status` given).

**Rationale:** Server-side filtering keeps one source of truth for "what matches" and lets the frontend show a correct loading state per request rather than fetching the whole table and filtering client-side (which also breaks the loading/empty-state model REQ-008 requires per query).

**Alternatives Rejected:**
1. Fetch all tasks once, filter/search in the browser — rejected: cannot produce a real per-query loading state, and silently stops matching correctly if the dataset grows beyond a single fetch's practical size (see DEFINE assumption A-002).

**Consequences:**
- Trade-off: every search keystroke (once debounced) is a network round trip.
- Benefit: filtering logic exists in exactly one place, and is exactly what the backend integration tests exercise.

---

### Decision 4: SQLite file path and schema creation lifecycle

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Status** | Accepted |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**Context:** Data must survive a restart of the application; the repo must stay clean of environment-specific binary artifacts.

**Choice:** SQLite file lives at `backend/data/taskflow.db` (path overridable via a `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` environment variable for tests); the directory is created on startup if missing; `Base.metadata.create_all(engine)` runs once at FastAPI startup (idempotent — safe to run every restart).

**Rationale:** A fixed on-disk path with `create_all` at startup satisfies "survive a restart" with zero migration tooling, matching Brainstorm Decision 1 (no Alembic — the schema is fixed for this build). Tests override `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` to a temp file so they never touch the real data file.

**Alternatives Rejected:**
1. In-memory SQLite (`:memory:`) as the default — rejected outright: fails the restart-persistence requirement (REQ-004) by definition.

**Consequences:**
- Trade-off: the DB file must be `.gitignore`d, or every run's data would appear in git status.
- Benefit: zero-configuration persistence; `rm backend/data/taskflow.db` is the entire "reset" procedure if ever needed manually.

## Code Patterns

### Pattern 1: FastAPI router + Pydantic schema + SQLAlchemy session (backend)

```python
# backend/app/routers/tasks.py — representative shape, not full implementation
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.database import get_db
from app.schemas import TaskCreate, TaskRead, TaskUpdate
from app import crud

router = APIRouter(prefix="/tasks", tags=["tasks"])


@router.get("", response_model=list[TaskRead])
def list_tasks(q: str | None = None, status: str | None = None, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return crud.list_tasks(db, search=q, status=status)


@router.post("", response_model=TaskRead, status_code=201)
def create_task(payload: TaskCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return crud.create_task(db, payload)


@router.patch("/{task_id}", response_model=TaskRead)
def update_task(task_id: str, payload: TaskUpdate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    task = crud.update_task(db, task_id, payload)
    if task is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Task not found")
    return task
```

### Pattern 2: Pydantic v2 validation (trim + length + enum)

```python
# backend/app/schemas.py — representative shape, not full implementation
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum

from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator


class TaskStatus(str, Enum):
    todo = "todo"
    doing = "doing"
    done = "done"


class TaskCreate(BaseModel):
    title: str
    description: str | None = None
    status: TaskStatus = TaskStatus.todo

    @field_validator("title")
    @classmethod
    def title_must_be_nonblank_and_bounded(cls, v: str) -> str:
        trimmed = v.strip()
        if not (1 <= len(trimmed) <= 120):
            raise ValueError("title must be 1-120 characters after trimming")
        return trimmed

    @field_validator("description")
    @classmethod
    def description_bounded(cls, v: str | None) -> str | None:
        if v is not None and len(v) > 500:
            raise ValueError("description must be at most 500 characters")
        return v
```

### Pattern 3: React data-fetching hook (frontend)

```typescript
// frontend/src/hooks/useTasks.ts — representative shape, not full implementation
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { listTasks } from "../api/client";
import type { Task, TaskStatus, ApiError } from "../types";

export function useTasks(query: string, status: TaskStatus | "all") {
  const [tasks, setTasks] = useState<Task[] | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [error, setError] = useState<ApiError | null>(null);

  const refetch = useCallback(async () => {
    setLoading(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      const result = await listTasks({ q: query || undefined, status: status === "all" ? undefined : status });
      setTasks(result);
    } catch (err) {
      setError(err as ApiError);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }, [query, status]);

  useEffect(() => {
    refetch();
  }, [refetch]);

  return { tasks, loading, error, refetch };
}
```

## Data Flow

```text
1. User types in SearchFilterBar or submits TaskForm / changes a TaskItem's status select
   │
   ▼
2. App.tsx / useTasks calls the typed API client (frontend/src/api/client.ts),
   which builds a query string / JSON body and issues fetch()
   │
   ▼
3. FastAPI router (backend/app/routers/tasks.py) receives the request;
   Pydantic validates the payload (schemas.py) — invalid input returns 422 here,
   before any DB access
   │
   ▼
4. crud.py builds a SQLAlchemy query/statement against the Task model
   and executes it through the session from database.py
   │
   ▼
5. SQLite file (backend/data/taskflow.db) is read/written; the row(s) affected
   are returned as ORM objects
   │
   ▼
6. FastAPI serializes the ORM objects via the TaskRead response_model back to JSON
   │
   ▼
7. The frontend hook updates {tasks, loading, error} state; components re-render
   the list, or the form shows the validation error, or an error banner appears
   on network/5xx failure — all without a page reload
```

The strategy covers every acceptance test in the DEFINE (AT-001 through AT-012): AT-001/006/007/008/009/010 map to backend integration tests; AT-002–005 map to backend unit tests (rejection) and frontend component tests (validation-state rendering); AT-011/AT-012 map to frontend component tests for the empty and request-failure states; the Playwright flow exercises AT-001, AT-007, AT-008, AT-009 together as a real user journey.

---

## Error Handling

| Error Type | Handling Strategy | Retry? |
|------------|-------------------|--------|
| Pydantic validation failure (bad title/description/status) | FastAPI returns 422 with a structured error body; frontend renders it as an inline validation-error state on the form | No |
| Task id not found (GET/PATCH/DELETE) | Router raises `HTTPException(404)`; frontend shows a not-found message for that action | No |
| Network failure / backend unreachable / 5xx | API client catches the fetch rejection or non-2xx status and returns a typed `ApiError`; frontend shows a top-level request-failure banner with a retry action | Yes — user-triggered retry via the same `refetch()` |
| Unexpected server exception | FastAPI's default 500 handler returns a generic JSON error; treated identically to the network-failure case on the frontend (no internal detail leaked) | No |

---

## Configuration

| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|------------|------|---------|--------------|
| `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` | string (env var) | `backend/data/taskflow.db` | SQLite file path; overridden to a temp path in tests |
| `TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` | string (env var, comma-separated) | `http://localhost:5173` | Origins allowed to call the API (the local Vite dev server) |
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | string (frontend env var) | `http://localhost:8000` | Base URL the frontend API client targets |

---

## Security Considerations

- No authentication/authorization is implemented — explicitly out of scope; the app is intended for a single local user on their own machine only, never exposed beyond `localhost`.
- All SQL is generated via SQLAlchemy's parameterized query construction — no string-formatted SQL anywhere, eliminating SQL injection risk (Decision 1).
- Pydantic validates and rejects malformed/oversized input before it reaches the database layer, bounding request-body size implicitly via the 120/500-character field limits.
- CORS is restricted to the known local dev origin via `TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` rather than left wide open (`*`).
- The SQLite file is `.gitignore`d so no local task data is ever committed to version control.

---

## Observability

| Aspect | Implementation |
|--------|----------------|
| Logging | FastAPI/Uvicorn's default structured access + error logging to stdout; no additional logging infrastructure needed for a local single-user tool |
| Metrics | None — out of scope; no operational metrics pipeline exists or is needed for a locally run tool with no deployment target |
| Tracing | None — out of scope for the same reason |

---

## Pipeline Architecture

Not applicable — TaskFlow is a single-table CRUD application, not a data pipeline, ETL process, or analytics workload. No DAG, partitioning, incremental strategy, or data-quality-gate sections apply.

# DEFINE: TaskFlow

> A locally runnable FastAPI + SQLite + React/TypeScript task manager with full CRUD, search, filter, and status workflow, validated inputs, and a restart-durable SQLite store.

## Metadata

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Feature** | TASKFLOW |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |
| **Author** | define-agent |
| **Status** | ✅ Complete (Built) |
| **Clarity Score** | 14/15 |

---

## Problem Statement

A single local user has no dependable, restart-durable way to create, organize, and track small tasks through a `todo → doing → done` workflow with search and filtering, without standing up authentication, multi-user infrastructure, or an external database.

---

## Target Users

| User | Role | Pain Point |
|------|------|------------|
| Single local user / developer | Runs the app on their own machine for personal task tracking | Needs a fast, dependable task list that survives restarts, works on any screen size, and gives clear feedback (loading/empty/error) — without needing an account, a server, or external infrastructure |

---

## Goals

What success looks like (prioritized):

| ID | Priority | Goal |
|----|----------|------|
| REQ-001 | **MUST** | Create, list, edit, and delete tasks via a JSON HTTP API |
| REQ-002 | **MUST** | Task status is one of `todo`/`doing`/`done` (default `todo`); a task can be moved between statuses |
| REQ-003 | **MUST** | Enforce field validation: title required after trim, 1–120 chars; description optional, ≤500 chars; status restricted to the three valid values |
| REQ-004 | **MUST** | Task data persists in SQLite and survives an application restart |
| REQ-005 | **MUST** | Search matches title and description, case-insensitively |
| REQ-006 | **MUST** | Filtering by status returns only tasks with the requested status |
| REQ-007 | **MUST** | Frontend works at desktop and mobile widths, performs all operations without page reloads, labels every interactive control accessibly, and visually distinguishes all three statuses |
| REQ-008 | **MUST** | Frontend exposes loading, empty, validation-error, and request-failure states |
| REQ-009 | **MUST** | Invalid input is rejected (whitespace-only title, title >120 chars, description >500 chars, unknown status) and a request for a missing task returns a not-found response |
| REQ-010 | **MUST** | Document supported runtime versions and exact clean install/run/test/lint/type-check/build commands |
| REQ-011 | **MUST** | Backend unit + integration tests, frontend component tests, and one browser end-to-end flow all exist and pass |
| REQ-012 | **MUST** | A CI workflow runs the documented checks (install, lint, type-check, test, build) on the feature branch |
| REQ-013 | **MUST** | Work lands on a feature branch with coherent commits, a clean working tree, and a root-level `PR.md` (title, summary, test evidence, risks, known limitations) |

> Requirement IDs are stable for the feature's whole life (Define → Design task manifest → Traceability Matrix → Build → PR). Never renumbered on iteration; appended only.

**Priority Guide:**
- **MUST** = MVP fails without this
- **SHOULD** = Important, but workaround exists
- **COULD** = Nice-to-have, cut first if needed

All thirteen goals are MUST: the governing brief states every one of them as a hard requirement or explicit invalid-input rule, and none has a documented workaround — there is no SHOULD/COULD tier for this feature (confirmed during Brainstorm's YAGNI pass, which is where every deferrable feature — auth, drag-and-drop, tags, pagination, etc. — was already removed from scope).

---

## Success Criteria

Measurable outcomes:

- [ ] 100% of the seven required operations (create, list, edit, delete, search, filter, move-status) are implemented and each has at least one passing automated test
- [ ] 0 of the 4 documented invalid-input cases (whitespace-only title, title >120 chars, description >500 chars, unknown status) are accepted by the API — each returns a 4xx with no row written
- [ ] A request for a non-existent task id returns a not-found (404) response in 100% of cases
- [ ] A dataset created before a backend process restart is present, unchanged, and fully queryable after the restart (0 data loss)
- [ ] Search and status-filter queries return exactly the matching subset (0 false positives/negatives) across at least the boundary cases: empty query, case-mismatched query, and each of the 3 status values
- [ ] The frontend renders correctly and remains operable at both a desktop width (e.g. 1280px) and a mobile width (e.g. 375px)
- [ ] All 4 required UI states (loading, empty, validation error, request failure) are reachable and visually distinct
- [ ] `install`, `run`, `test`, `lint`, `type-check`, and `build` each succeed as a single documented command for both backend and frontend
- [ ] CI runs all documented checks and passes on the feature branch

---

## Acceptance Tests

| ID | Scenario | Given | When | Then |
|----|----------|-------|------|------|
| AT-001 | Create a task (happy path) | No prior state needed | User submits a title of 1–120 trimmed chars (description optional) | A task is created with `status=todo`, a stable id, and `created_at`/`updated_at` timestamps; it appears in the list |
| AT-002 | Reject whitespace-only title | — | User submits a title of only spaces/tabs | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
| AT-003 | Reject title over 120 chars | — | User submits a 121-character title | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
| AT-004 | Reject description over 500 chars | — | User submits a 501-character description | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
| AT-005 | Reject unknown status | — | User submits `status="archived"` (or any value outside todo/doing/done) | API returns a validation error; no task is created |
| AT-006 | Not-found on missing task | A task id that does not exist in the store | User requests, edits, or deletes that id | API returns a 404 (not-found) response |
| AT-007 | Move a task between statuses | A task exists with `status=todo` | User edits the task's status to `doing`, then to `done` | The task's status updates each time; `updated_at` changes; the task appears under the correct status filter after each move |
| AT-008 | Case-insensitive search | Tasks exist titled "Buy Milk" and "Read Book" | User searches for `"MILK"` | Only "Buy Milk" is returned |
| AT-009 | Status filter isolation | Tasks exist in all three statuses | User filters by `status=doing` | Only `doing` tasks are returned; `todo` and `done` tasks are excluded |
| AT-010 | Restart persistence | At least one task has been created | The backend process is stopped and restarted | The previously created task(s) are still present and unchanged via `GET` |
| AT-011 | Frontend empty state | No tasks exist (or a search/filter matches none) | User loads the app or applies a non-matching search/filter | An accessible empty-state message is shown instead of a blank list or error |
| AT-012 | Frontend request-failure state | The backend is unreachable or returns a 5xx | User performs any operation | An accessible error/failure state is shown instead of a silent failure or crash |

---

## Out of Scope

Explicitly NOT included in this feature:

- Authentication, user accounts, or any multi-user/shared-ownership behavior
- Deployment configuration, containerization, or hosting of any kind
- Any external database engine (Postgres, MySQL, etc.) — SQLite only
- Drag-and-drop Kanban board interaction (status changes via a labeled control instead)
- Tags/labels, priorities, due dates, bulk operations, pagination, real-time sync (WebSockets/polling), dark mode/theming
- Inspecting or copying application code or planning artifacts from any other implementation or repository

---

## Constraints

| Type | Constraint | Impact |
|------|------------|--------|
| Technical | Backend must be Python + FastAPI + SQLite; frontend must be React + TypeScript; API must be JSON over HTTP | Fixes the technology stack outright; Design phase selects concrete libraries within these bounds (ORM, build tool, test frameworks) |
| Technical | No authentication, multi-user behavior, deployment, or external database | Removes entire categories of design surface (auth middleware, session storage, infra-as-code, connection pooling to a networked DB) |
| Process | Must not inspect the other benchmark implementation or copy code/artifacts from outside this repository | Every file in this build must be authored fresh, grounded only in this repository's own context and this DEFINE document |
| Process | Must not create or publish a GitHub repository or pull request | `PR.md` is the deliverable, not an actual GitHub PR; no `gh pr create` or repo creation at any point |
| Environment | The `.claude/` directory tree is write-protected in this environment | SDD artifacts are kept at repo-root `sdd/` instead of `.claude/sdd/` (see Brainstorm decision log) |
| Timeline | No explicit deadline stated in the governing brief | Scope is bounded by completeness against the brief rather than a date; YAGNI keeps effort proportionate |

---

## Technical Context

> Essential context for Design phase — prevents misplaced files and missed infrastructure needs.

| Aspect | Value | Notes |
|--------|-------|-------|
| **Deployment Location** | Repo root, split into `backend/` (FastAPI + SQLite) and `frontend/` (React + TypeScript + Vite) | Clean separation; each half owns its own dependency manifest, test runner, and lint/type-check config |
| **KB Domains** | None applicable | The plugin KB (`kb/_index.yaml`) covers data-engineering domains only (dbt, Spark, Airflow, lakehouse, streaming); no web-application/FastAPI/React domain exists. Design will proceed on general framework-standard practice rather than a cited KB pattern (confidence 0.70, per Brainstorm) |
| **IaC Impact** | None | Deployment and infrastructure are explicitly out of scope |

**Why This Matters:**

- **Location** → Design phase uses correct project structure, prevents misplaced files
- **KB Domains** → No domain-specific patterns to pull; Design instead follows current FastAPI/React ecosystem conventions (SQLAlchemy 2.0, Pydantic v2, Vite, Vitest/RTL, Playwright) as selected in Brainstorm's Approach A
- **IaC Impact** → Confirmed none needed; avoids over-building infrastructure this feature doesn't require

---

## Data Contract

Not applicable — this feature is a single-table CRUD application (`tasks`), not a data pipeline, ETL process, or analytics workload. No source systems, freshness SLAs, or lineage requirements apply.

# DESIGN: TaskFlow

> Technical design for implementing TaskFlow — a locally runnable FastAPI + SQLite + React/TypeScript task manager

## Metadata

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Feature** | TASKFLOW |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |
| **Author** | design-agent |
| **DEFINE** | [DEFINE_TASKFLOW.md](./DEFINE_TASKFLOW.md) |
| **Risk Level** | low — echoed from DEFINE: single local process/user, no auth surface, ORM-parameterized queries, no destructive migration, git-ignored SQLite file, all changes reversible via git |
| **Status** | ✅ Complete (Built) |

---

## Architecture Overview

```text
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                              SYSTEM DIAGRAM                                │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│   ┌─────────────────────────┐        JSON/HTTP        ┌─────────────────┐ │
│   │   Browser (desktop or   │  ───────────────────►   │   FastAPI app   │ │
│   │   mobile viewport)      │   GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE │   (uvicorn)     │ │
│   │                         │  ◄───────────────────   │                 │ │
│   │  React + TypeScript SPA │        JSON responses   │  APIRouter:     │ │
│   │  ┌───────────────────┐  │                          │  /tasks         │ │
│   │  │ SearchFilterBar   │  │                          │  /tasks/{id}    │ │
│   │  │ TaskForm          │  │                          └────────┬────────┘ │
│   │  │ TaskList/TaskItem │  │                                   │          │
│   │  │ Loading/Empty/    │  │                          Pydantic v2 schemas │
│   │  │ Error states      │  │                          (validate in/out)   │
│   │  └───────────────────┘  │                                   │          │
│   └─────────────────────────┘                          SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM  │
│                                                                   │          │
│                                                                   ▼          │
│                                                          ┌─────────────────┐ │
│                                                          │  SQLite file    │ │
│                                                          │  backend/data/  │ │
│                                                          │  taskflow.db    │ │
│                                                          │  (persists      │ │
│                                                          │   across        │ │
│                                                          │   restarts)     │ │
│                                                          └─────────────────┘ │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Components

| Component | Purpose | Technology |
|-----------|---------|------------|
| FastAPI app (`backend/app/main.py`) | HTTP entry point, CORS for the local Vite dev server, startup schema creation | Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Uvicorn |
| Task router (`backend/app/routers/tasks.py`) | REST endpoints: list (with search/filter), create, get, update, delete | FastAPI `APIRouter`, dependency-injected DB session |
| Schemas (`backend/app/schemas.py`) | Request/response validation: trim + length limits on title/description, status enum, timestamp serialization | Pydantic v2 |
| Models + DB session (`backend/app/models.py`, `backend/app/database.py`) | `Task` ORM mapping to the `tasks` table; SQLite engine/session factory | SQLAlchemy 2.0 (declarative + `Session`) |
| CRUD layer (`backend/app/crud.py`) | Query construction: case-insensitive search (`LIKE` on lowered columns), status filter, create/update/delete logic, `updated_at` bump | SQLAlchemy Core expressions |
| React SPA (`frontend/src/`) | Single page: search/filter bar, task list, create/edit form, per-task status control, loading/empty/validation/error states | React 18, TypeScript, Vite |
| API client (`frontend/src/api/client.ts`) | Typed `fetch` wrapper: builds query strings, parses JSON, normalizes error shapes | TypeScript, native `fetch` |
| Backend test suite (`backend/tests/`) | Unit tests (schema validation) + integration tests (full API via `TestClient`, temp SQLite file) | pytest, `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` |
| Frontend test suite (`frontend/src/**/*.test.tsx`) | Component tests: rendering, form validation feedback, state transitions, accessibility roles | Vitest, React Testing Library |
| E2E suite (`frontend/e2e/`) | One full browser flow: create → search → filter → move status → delete, against the real backend | Playwright |
| CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) | Runs install/lint/type-check/test/build for both halves on every push/PR | GitHub Actions |

---

## Key Decisions

### Decision 1: SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM + Pydantic v2 for persistence and validation

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Status** | Accepted |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**Context:** The backend must persist tasks in SQLite and enforce exact field constraints (title 1–120 trimmed, description ≤500, status enum) with no external database and no KB pattern to draw from (confirmed in Brainstorm: no FastAPI/React domain in this plugin's KB).

**Choice:** Use SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative models as the single source of schema truth, with Pydantic v2 `BaseModel` schemas (`TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskRead`) for request/response validation, wired through FastAPI's `response_model` and dependency-injected sessions.

**Rationale:** SQLAlchemy guarantees parameterized queries (no hand-built SQL to audit for injection); Pydantic v2's `Field(min_length=1, max_length=120)` plus a `field_validator` for trimming maps directly onto the brief's exact numeric constraints and produces structured 422 error bodies the frontend can render as validation state.

**Alternatives Rejected:**
1. Raw `sqlite3` + hand-written SQL — rejected because every query becomes a manual injection-audit surface with no compile-time schema guarantee (Brainstorm Approach B).
2. SQLModel — rejected as an unnecessary extra abstraction layer for a single-table schema; SQLAlchemy directly is more mature and no less code here (Brainstorm Approach C, partial).

**Consequences:**
- Trade-off: one more dependency (`sqlalchemy`) beyond the stdlib.
- Benefit: schema, validation, and query safety all come from well-tested, idiomatic libraries rather than custom code that must be independently verified in review.

---

### Decision 2: Status changes via `PATCH /tasks/{id}`, not a dedicated transition endpoint

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Status** | Accepted |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**Context:** The brief requires the ability to move a task between `todo`/`doing`/`done` alongside ordinary field edits (title, description).

**Choice:** Expose a single `PATCH /tasks/{id}` endpoint accepting any subset of `{title, description, status}`; moving a task is just a `PATCH` with `{"status": "doing"}`.

**Rationale:** The brief describes status change as one of several editable attributes, not a distinct workflow with transition guards, history, or side effects. A single partial-update endpoint covers every "edit" requirement (REQ-001) and the "move" requirement (REQ-002) with one code path to validate and test.

**Alternatives Rejected:**
1. Separate `POST /tasks/{id}/move` endpoint — rejected: adds a second code path and a second set of tests for behavior that is identical to a field edit once validation passes.

**Consequences:**
- Trade-off: the API does not model status transitions as a guarded state machine (e.g., cannot forbid `done → todo` even if a future spec wanted that).
- Benefit: one endpoint, one validation path, fewer places for the 4 invalid-input rules to be enforced inconsistently.

---

### Decision 3: Search and filter as server-side query parameters on `GET /tasks`

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Status** | Accepted |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**Context:** Search must match title/description case-insensitively; filtering must return only the requested status; both must compose (a search within a status).

**Choice:** `GET /tasks?q=<term>&status=<todo|doing|done>` — both optional, combinable, evaluated in SQLAlchemy as `WHERE lower(title) LIKE lower(:q) OR lower(description) LIKE lower(:q)` (when `q` given) `AND status = :status` (when `status` given).

**Rationale:** Server-side filtering keeps one source of truth for "what matches" and lets the frontend show a correct loading state per request rather than fetching the whole table and filtering client-side (which also breaks the loading/empty-state model REQ-008 requires per query).

**Alternatives Rejected:**
1. Fetch all tasks once, filter/search in the browser — rejected: cannot produce a real per-query loading state, and silently stops matching correctly if the dataset grows beyond a single fetch's practical size (see DEFINE assumption A-002).

**Consequences:**
- Trade-off: every search keystroke (once debounced) is a network round trip.
- Benefit: filtering logic exists in exactly one place, and is exactly what the backend integration tests exercise.

---

### Decision 4: SQLite file path and schema creation lifecycle

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Status** | Accepted |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**Context:** Data must survive a restart of the application; the repo must stay clean of environment-specific binary artifacts.

**Choice:** SQLite file lives at `backend/data/taskflow.db` (path overridable via a `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` environment variable for tests); the directory is created on startup if missing; `Base.metadata.create_all(engine)` runs once at FastAPI startup (idempotent — safe to run every restart).

**Rationale:** A fixed on-disk path with `create_all` at startup satisfies "survive a restart" with zero migration tooling, matching Brainstorm Decision 1 (no Alembic — the schema is fixed for this build). Tests override `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` to a temp file so they never touch the real data file.

**Alternatives Rejected:**
1. In-memory SQLite (`:memory:`) as the default — rejected outright: fails the restart-persistence requirement (REQ-004) by definition.

**Consequences:**
- Trade-off: the DB file must be `.gitignore`d, or every run's data would appear in git status.
- Benefit: zero-configuration persistence; `rm backend/data/taskflow.db` is the entire "reset" procedure if ever needed manually.

## Code Patterns

### Pattern 1: FastAPI router + Pydantic schema + SQLAlchemy session (backend)

```python
# backend/app/routers/tasks.py — representative shape, not full implementation
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.database import get_db
from app.schemas import TaskCreate, TaskRead, TaskUpdate
from app import crud

router = APIRouter(prefix="/tasks", tags=["tasks"])


@router.get("", response_model=list[TaskRead])
def list_tasks(q: str | None = None, status: str | None = None, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return crud.list_tasks(db, search=q, status=status)


@router.post("", response_model=TaskRead, status_code=201)
def create_task(payload: TaskCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return crud.create_task(db, payload)


@router.patch("/{task_id}", response_model=TaskRead)
def update_task(task_id: str, payload: TaskUpdate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    task = crud.update_task(db, task_id, payload)
    if task is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Task not found")
    return task
```

### Pattern 2: Pydantic v2 validation (trim + length + enum)

```python
# backend/app/schemas.py — representative shape, not full implementation
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum

from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator


class TaskStatus(str, Enum):
    todo = "todo"
    doing = "doing"
    done = "done"


class TaskCreate(BaseModel):
    title: str
    description: str | None = None
    status: TaskStatus = TaskStatus.todo

    @field_validator("title")
    @classmethod
    def title_must_be_nonblank_and_bounded(cls, v: str) -> str:
        trimmed = v.strip()
        if not (1 <= len(trimmed) <= 120):
            raise ValueError("title must be 1-120 characters after trimming")
        return trimmed

    @field_validator("description")
    @classmethod
    def description_bounded(cls, v: str | None) -> str | None:
        if v is not None and len(v) > 500:
            raise ValueError("description must be at most 500 characters")
        return v
```

```typescript
  const [tasks, setTasks] = useState<Task[] | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [error, setError] = useState<ApiError | null>(null);

  const refetch = useCallback(async () => {
    setLoading(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      const result = await listTasks({ q: query || undefined, status: status === "all" ? undefined : status });
      setTasks(result);
    } catch (err) {
      setError(err as ApiError);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }, [query, status]);

  useEffect(() => {
    refetch();
  }, [refetch]);

  return { tasks, loading, error, refetch };
}
```

---

## Data Flow

```text
1. User types in SearchFilterBar or submits TaskForm / changes a TaskItem's status select
   │
   ▼
2. App.tsx / useTasks calls the typed API client (frontend/src/api/client.ts),
   which builds a query string / JSON body and issues fetch()
   │
   ▼
3. FastAPI router (backend/app/routers/tasks.py) receives the request;
   Pydantic validates the payload (schemas.py) — invalid input returns 422 here,
   before any DB access
   │
   ▼
4. crud.py builds a SQLAlchemy query/statement against the Task model
   and executes it through the session from database.py
   │
   ▼
5. SQLite file (backend/data/taskflow.db) is read/written; the row(s) affected
   are returned as ORM objects
   │
   ▼
6. FastAPI serializes the ORM objects via the TaskRead response_model back to JSON
   │
   ▼
7. The frontend hook updates {tasks, loading, error} state; components re-render
   the list, or the form shows the validation error, or an error banner appears
   on network/5xx failure — all without a page reload
```

---

## Integration Points

| External System | Integration Type | Authentication |
|-----------------|-----------------|----------------|
| None | — | — |

No external systems are integrated — the only "integration" is the frontend SPA calling its own co-located FastAPI backend over local HTTP, which is the core architecture itself rather than an external dependency. This is intentional per the DEFINE's constraints (no auth, no external DB, no deployment).

---

## Testing Strategy

| Test Type | Scope | Files | Tools | Coverage Goal |
|-----------|-------|-------|-------|---------------|
| Unit | Pydantic schema validation boundaries (title/description/status) | `backend/tests/test_schemas.py` | pytest | Every boundary in DEFINE AT-002–AT-005 |
| Integration | Full API behavior against a real (temp-file) SQLite DB | `backend/tests/test_tasks_api.py` | pytest + `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` | Every acceptance test AT-001, AT-006–AT-010 |
| Component | Frontend rendering, validation feedback, state transitions, accessible queries | `frontend/src/components/*.test.tsx` | Vitest + React Testing Library | AT-002–AT-005 (validation UI), AT-011, AT-012 (empty/failure states) |
| E2E | One full browser journey: create → search → filter → move status → delete | `frontend/e2e/taskflow.spec.ts` | Playwright | AT-001, AT-007, AT-008, AT-009 combined in one flow |

The strategy covers every acceptance test in the DEFINE (AT-001 through AT-012): AT-001/006/007/008/009/010 map to backend integration tests; AT-002–005 map to backend unit tests (rejection) and frontend component tests (validation-state rendering); AT-011/AT-012 map to frontend component tests for the empty and request-failure states; the Playwright flow exercises AT-001, AT-007, AT-008, AT-009 together as a real user journey.

---

## Error Handling

| Error Type | Handling Strategy | Retry? |
|------------|-------------------|--------|
| Pydantic validation failure (bad title/description/status) | FastAPI returns 422 with a structured error body; frontend renders it as an inline validation-error state on the form | No |
| Task id not found (GET/PATCH/DELETE) | Router raises `HTTPException(404)`; frontend shows a not-found message for that action | No |
| Network failure / backend unreachable / 5xx | API client catches the fetch rejection or non-2xx status and returns a typed `ApiError`; frontend shows a top-level request-failure banner with a retry action | Yes — user-triggered retry via the same `refetch()` |
| Unexpected server exception | FastAPI's default 500 handler returns a generic JSON error; treated identically to the network-failure case on the frontend (no internal detail leaked) | No |

---

## Configuration

| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|------------|------|---------|--------------|
| `TASKFLOW_DB_PATH` | string (env var) | `backend/data/taskflow.db` | SQLite file path; overridden to a temp path in tests |
| `TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` | string (env var, comma-separated) | `http://localhost:5173` | Origins allowed to call the API (the local Vite dev server) |
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | string (frontend env var) | `http://localhost:8000` | Base URL the frontend API client targets |

---

## Security Considerations

- No authentication/authorization is implemented — explicitly out of scope; the app is intended for a single local user on their own machine only, never exposed beyond `localhost`.
- All SQL is generated via SQLAlchemy's parameterized query construction — no string-formatted SQL anywhere, eliminating SQL injection risk (Decision 1).
- Pydantic validates and rejects malformed/oversized input before it reaches the database layer, bounding request-body size implicitly via the 120/500-character field limits.
- CORS is restricted to the known local dev origin via `TASKFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS` rather than left wide open (`*`).
- The SQLite file is `.gitignore`d so no local task data is ever committed to version control.

---

## Observability

| Aspect | Implementation |
|--------|----------------|
| Logging | FastAPI/Uvicorn's default structured access + error logging to stdout; no additional logging infrastructure needed for a local single-user tool |
| Metrics | None — out of scope; no operational metrics pipeline exists or is needed for a locally run tool with no deployment target |
| Tracing | None — out of scope for the same reason |

---

## Pipeline Architecture

Not applicable — TaskFlow is a single-table CRUD application, not a data pipeline, ETL process, or analytics workload. No DAG, partitioning, incremental strategy, or data-quality-gate sections apply.

---

## Revision History

| Version | Date | Author | Changes |
|---------|------|--------|---------|
| 1.0 | 2026-07-30 | design-agent | Initial version, derived from `sdd/features/DEFINE_TASKFLOW.md` |

---

## Next Step

**Ready for:** `/build sdd/features/DESIGN_TASKFLOW.md`

263	(`SHIPPED_TEMPLATE.md` owns the table shape — no improvised sections),
264	feeding the lessons learned. Consume `null` values as-is — a

266	never backfilled at ship time.
267

269	recalibration, no budget adjustment, no gate tuning happens because a metric
270	moved — that requires multiple comparable runs AND human review, outside any
271	single ship. Ship reports numbers; humans change policy.
272

274	
275	When the archive is complete, report closure to the user:
276	
277	| Handoff item | Content |
278	|--------------|---------|
279	| **Archive location** | `.claude/sdd/archive/{FEATURE}/` with the full artifact list |
280	| **SHIPPED document** | Path to `SHIPPED_{DATE}.md` + one-line summary of what shipped |
281	| **Lessons headline** | The 2-3 most actionable lessons captured |
282	| **Statuses** | Confirmation that DEFINE, DESIGN, and BUILD_REPORT now read "✅ Shipped" |
283	| **Workspace** | `features/` and `reports/` clean of this feature's working files |
284	| **Next step** | Start the next feature with `/define` (or `/brainstorm` for an unshaped idea) |
285

288	## Anti-Patterns
289	
290	| Never Do | Why | Instead |
291	|----------|-----|---------|
292	| Ship with failing tests | Broken code archived | Fix tests first — route back to `/build` |
293	| Ship incomplete builds | Missing functionality | Complete build first |
294	| Vague lessons learned | Not actionable | Be specific and concrete |
295	| Skip artifact verification | May be incomplete | Always verify all exist |
296	| Leave working files | Clutter | Clean up after archive |
297	| Re-inline the SHIPPED format | Drifts from the template | Follow `SHIPPED_TEMPLATE.md` |
298	
299	---

303	- Template: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/sdd/templates/SHIPPED_TEMPLATE.md`
304	- Contracts: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/sdd/architecture/WORKFLOW_CONTRACTS.yaml`
305	- Executor: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/agents/workflow/ship-agent.md`
306	- Entrypoint: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/commands/workflow/ship.md`
307	- Previous phase: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/commands/workflow/build.md`
